name: True the Vote
subject: We're going old school — are you ready?
body:
What we're doing now and where we're headed soon
| | | November 09, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/5que5omwrvf7h0pxpr6b6h99xe3p3snhg0mpo/6qheh8hl43qdv7iohk/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvbjR1b2h2aGd3cXd6N2g3cTMzOXFlaDY2NDlrZ210bGhxdm4yMw==) | |
---
|
### **From Catherine**
[**Support True the Vote’s work**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/5que5omwrvf7h0pxpr6b6h99xe3p3snhg0mpo/kkhmh6hnpo73gnilh7/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl) Hi Friend — Well, it was a difficult week. I wish I could sit across the table from you today and just talk. I would want to hear how you’re doing. What you’re thinking. What these last few days have been like for you. And I would want to thank you, personally, for everything you have poured into this country. Some of you have been with us for years. Some found us more recently, through Scan. Check. Protect. or 7 Votes. You checked your records, called your friends, served in elections, prayed, gave, and stood in an unnecessary gap created by a political machine with too little leadership and too much hubris. And now here we are. But even though these are tough times, the fact is, in your heart of hearts, you know, we have to keep showing up. Even in the worst of times, America remains the greatest country in the world because of her people. There is goodness here. Courage. Ingenuity. Faith. People who will give the shirt off their backs and then ask what else you need. And what we need — what we’re going to do — is to go old school. Our liberty is literally at risk. We have a responsibility to protect it, and I believe we still can. But before we get into what ‘old school True the Vote’ means, first, let’s talk about what we know, and what we are still waiting to learn, about Tuesday’s election.
### **What Are We Waiting On?**
Though the anomalies are clear, any serious assessment of whether outcomes were legitimate must include knowing _who_ voted. Counting the votes may give us “winners,” but considering how error-riddled the voter rolls are and how porous our overall electoral process is, nothing should be taken for granted. The only way we can even approach answering the question of whether or not it was an accurate election is to see _who_ voted and whether or not the voters who cast votes were eligible to do so. Of course, it’s only one of many, many issues that must be considered, but it is the key. Who voted? And the question of “when we will know who voted” is one of the many breakdowns in a process that seems to be perpetually (some might say, intentionally) broken. Because we will only know who voted after certification, after it is, realistically, too late. By design. Yes, a state will certify its election long before it will release its records of who voted, making it almost impossible for groups like ours, or plaintiffs in court cases, to make their arguments. Here’s a look at how the dates will likely shake out in a few states, with the certification dates shown alongside our estimates for comparable voter-history updates: | State | Certification date or deadline | Estimated voter-history update*
---|---|---
Arizona | Certification: November 23, 2026 — statewide canvass. | Voter-history update*: Around December 16, 2026
Georgia | Certification: By November 20, 2026 — state certification. | Voter-history update*: Around December 2, 2026
Michigan | Certification: By November 23, 2026 — state canvass. | Voter-history update*: Around December 16, 2026
Nevada | Certification: November 24, 2026 — statewide canvass. | Voter-history update*: Around December 2, 2026
North Carolina | Certification: November 24, 2026 — state canvass. | Voter-history update*: Around December 16, 2026
Pennsylvania | Certification: Counties certify by November 23, 2026. State certification follows; no separate fixed statewide date. | Voter-history update*: Around February 3, 2027
Wisconsin | Certification: By December 1, 2026 — state certification. | Voter-history update*: Around February 3, 2027
Texas | Certification: November 21–December 7, 2026 — ordinary state canvass. Governor and lieutenant governor follow a separate process. | Voter-history update*: Around December 16, 2026
_Certification dates reflect scheduled canvasses or ordinary deadlines; recounts, litigation, and runoffs can affect particular contests. Note: Texas’s governor and lieutenant governor results are canvassed separately by the Legislature after it convenes January 12, 2027._
_* Voter-history availability estimates apply the same number of days after Election Day as published updates were in 2022 and 2024. Records may appear earlier, and updates may continue afterward._
We will examine what becomes available, pursue the questions the evidence raises, and share what we can establish.
But one thing we can establish without wasting another day is that our approach must change.
**And so, True the Vote is going old school.**
We are getting out from behind our keyboards and cameras and going town to town. I want to sit in a room with you. Hear what is happening where you live. Meet the people who are willing to help. Work through what we can do together, and find our way back to an America we can put our hope in.
In one of Gregg Phillips’s ‘[Patriot Games](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/5que5omwrvf7h0pxpr6b6h99xe3p3snhg0mpo/58hvh7hgw4ezpkc6h4/aHR0cHM6Ly9ydW1ibGUuY29tL3Y3aHl6aDItdGhlLXZvdGUtaXMtcHJlY2lvdXMtd2h5LXlvdS1zaG91bGQtc2hvdy11cC5odG1s)’ podcasts this week, he talked about drawing inspiration from Abraham Lincoln’s organizing plans from 1840: make a “perfect list” of voters, organize small local groups, speak with people face to face, follow up, and see the work through.
Nearly two centuries later, there is still something powerful about a person who knows your name, looks you in the eye, and stands with you in a shared understanding of what is at stake.
That is the spirit we will bring to this next chapter.
In many ways, it’s going back to where we came from. Back in the early years of True the Vote, we helped support hundreds of groups all over the country. Over the years (and the lawsuits), we stopped organizing groups, stopped our webinars, weekly calls, and annual summits.
Instead, we pivoted to building the tech that was desperately needed to support election integrity advocates. And now, that work is done. We have a complete toolkit to offer all volunteers.
We also took on enormous research projects in 2020. We helped Georgia citizens file voter challenges in a statewide effort that led to a lawsuit that continues to this day.
We also worked with geospatial data that was later used in “2000 Mules,” which also resulted in a lawsuit over the movie.
We also exposed Konnech, an election software company that was running election operations for some of the largest counties in America out of its offices in Beijing. That effort also resulted in a lawsuit and prison time. Gregg Phillips and I were released by an emergency order of the U.S. Court of Appeals.
So, we’ve been through a lot. But that was then and this is now.
And now is the time to go back to how True the Vote first began. Person to person, in person.
Will you join us?
Together, we can work in local elections, study and work to shore up the very broken process we have, and advocate for common-sense reform. We will meet regularly, share what we learn, and prepare others to lead.
Does this sound like something you would want to be part of?
True the Vote will bring our tools, training, and experience. You bring something we could never build from a distance: your knowledge of your hometown and your relationships with the people who live there (and if you don’t have relationships, we can build them together).
**Beginning in January 2027, we will hold weekly calls. And we will come to you.**
We will work with local hosts to bring people together, town by town. We will build the resources to reach more places and train more people. We will scale by helping one another become capable of carrying the work.
Picture what that could mean a year from now.
People in your community who know one another and know what to do. Someone to call when a neighbor needs help. More citizens prepared to serve. Questions followed through to answers. A better process built through steady, patient work.
And friendships formed along the way. We need that, too.
We need to help each other be human — to listen, to laugh, to work through disagreements, to remember that there is a person on the other side of the conversation. We need a shared true north: truth, liberty, responsibility, and care for the country our children will inherit.
I believe God has placed work in front of us that we are capable of doing. It is our call. And it is the only way.
**Never mistake an imperfect system for a powerless people. We are powerful, together.**
If you are ready to be part of this next chapter, just email us at [**info@truethevote.org**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/5que5omwrvf7h0pxpr6b6h99xe3p3snhg0mpo/g3hnh5hm20vk7gcrh9/bWFpbHRvOmluZm9AdHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3Jn) and say:
**I’m in.**
We’ll keep asking from now till ... well, for the foreseeable future, so please invite your friends. And we’ll start with weekly calls in January. You do not have to arrive with all the answers. Bring your willingness. We will learn, work, and build together.
If you think this call is for you, it is. Let’s go. For God and Country.
Isaiah 6:8. Ephesians 6. Keep the faith. Never quit.
Ever onward —

---
P.S. This Thursday marked four years since Gregg and I were released from the ICE Prison in Conroe, Texas. To everyone who prayed for us during that time, thank you. What a journey, then and now. All to His glory.
P.P.S. [If you can help support our work, please do.](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/5que5omwrvf7h0pxpr6b6h99xe3p3snhg0mpo/kkhmh6hnpo73gnilh7/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl) We appreciate your help more than you can know!

| | | Peter, **Votes are still being counted in Alaska.** Right now, just hundreds of votes separate Senator Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola. Out of every ballot cast across the whole state, it comes down to a few hundred. That’s not a lead. _That’s a coin flip._ Here’s what makes my blood boil: Democrats played a dirty trick in this race. They recruited a second “Dan Sullivan” to get on the ballot, a fake candidate with the same name with ties to the Democrats meant to confuse voters and pull votes away from the real one. _And it worked well enough to matter_. If the fake weren’t in this race, Dan would be leading right now. I knew what they were up to. That’s why I got on a plane and went to Alaska to campaign for Dan BEFORE Election Day.

In the blink of an eye, two million acres of pristine canyons, ancient cliff dwellings, and sacred tribal sites were deleted from the map and handed straight to the uranium and coal lobbies. The politicians who stood on stage and cheered for this fire sale are banking on one specific thing: your exhaustion. They want you to look at the sheer scale of this corporate giveaway, feel completely overwhelmed by the news cycle, and decide it's not worth fighting back. They think their billionaire donors have already written the checks to make this a permanent victory. But they severely miscalculated. We can prove them wrong for less than the cost of a cheap cup of coffee. ~ ~~ They think they can quietly liquidate two million acres of our history behind closed doors. body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=22%2E6803%2Eg2J2jl)
Hi,
We know last week’s election gave us a lot to celebrate, but we need your help to stop Congress from sneaking a dangerous bill through right under our noses. Congress is considering legislation to gut our most important environmental protections, and shockingly, Democrats are helping lead the charge **[We need you to call your Senators today and urge them to stop this dangerous legislation before it’s too late.](https://act.janepac.com/go/55?t=3&akid=22%2E6803%2Eg2J2jl)**
**[Write your letter ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/55?t=4&akid=22%2E6803%2Eg2J2jl)**
The bill is called the _Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA)_ , but don't let the name fool you. It would gut laws protecting our air, water, wildlife, and public lands and give polluters sweeping rights to sue the government if they don’t get what they want.
This dangerous bill would speed up permitting for fossil fuel companies, mining corporations, and Big Tech and allow them to bulldoze environmental safeguards, undermine Tribal sovereignty, and silence local communities. **It would also lock in the Trump Administration's fossil fuels approvals, and give them carte blanche to approve new devastating projects over the next two years.**
Sadly, this isn’t just some MAGA project. Democratic Senators Martin Heinrich (NM) and Sheldon Whitehouse (RI) are sponsoring and advancing this legislation, even as Donald Trump and his party wage an all out assault on our environment.
**The clock is ticking.** We cannot let Congress use what should be the lamest of lame-duck sessions to gut environmental protections and hand Big Oil a victory with such far reaching implications.
**[Will you write your Senators and urge them to oppose this fossil fuel giveaway before it’s too late?](https://act.janepac.com/go/55?t=5&akid=22%2E6803%2Eg2J2jl)**
**To be clear, this is not a run-of-the-mill compromise bill,** it’s a seismic shift that changes the role of our government from protecting the public from corporations to protecting corporations from oversight.
This bill would permanently erode protections found in laws like the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act, National Historic Preservation Act, and Endangered Species Act that have protected our drinking water, public lands, and Tribal cultural sites. And it would make it almost impossible to challenge dangerous development projects, locking in long-term damage to our communities.
All of this only serves to fast-track fossil fuel infrastructure and power-hungry AI data centers while leaving nearby residents to bear the consequences.
Proponents say this will help expand alternative energy. This isn’t offering clean energy a helping hand. **It's a corporate handout.**
**[Will you write your Senators today and demand they protect our planet instead of tossing so much hard-earned progress out the window?](https://act.janepac.com/go/55?t=6&akid=22%2E6803%2Eg2J2jl)**
**[Click here to write your letters – it will only take a minute or two.](https://act.janepac.com/go/55?t=7&akid=22%2E6803%2Eg2J2jl)** You can use the provided talking points, or speak from your heart and tell them why we must stop this bill.
Onward,
JanePAC Advocacy Team

This dangerous bill would speed up permitting for fossil fuel companies, mining corporations, and Big Tech and allow them to bulldoze environmental safeguards, undermine Tribal sovereignty, and silence local communities. It would also lock in the Trump Administration's fossil fuels approvals, and give them carte blanche to approve new devastating projects over the next two years. Sadly, this isn’t just some MAGA project. Democratic Senators Martin Heinrich (NM) and Sheldon Whitehouse (RI) are sponsoring and advancing this legislation, even as Donald Trump and his party wage an all out assault on our environment. The clock is ticking. We cannot let Congress use what should be the lamest of lame-duck sessions to gut environmental protections and hand Big Oil a victory with such far reaching implications. To be clear, this is not a run-of-the-mill compromise bill, it’s a seismic shift that changes the role of our government from protecting the public from corporations to protecting corporations from oversight. This bill would permanently erode protections found in laws like the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act, National Historic Preservation Act, and Endangered Species Act that have protected our drinking water, public lands, and Tribal cultural sites. And it would make it almost impossible to challenge dangerous development projects, locking in long-term damage to our communities. All of this only serves to fast-track fossil fuel infrastructure and power-hungry AI data centers while leaving nearby residents to bear the consequences. Proponents say this will help expand alternative energy. This isn’t offering clean energy a helping hand. It's a corporate handout. You can use the provided talking points, or speak from your heart and tell them why we must stop this bill. Onward, JanePAC Advocacy Team | ---|--- | | | | ---|---|---|---|---

## Study: 1 in 6 TN Households in the Red

## VDOT Eyes 2-Way I-95 Express Lanes
The Virginia Department of Transportation is studying whether to run the I-95 Express Lanes [_in both directions around the clock_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SqzAMhZ_GdM7YivkrXNyGLrfdklGwDJp1MAMKbN5-h8zuE2wraXTO933c-hty4nn8jw_yssd-pmNLJEJrz21JX8tK25Zwpk2e4SX5OU7Ug4FKW6tN2-MgvFPvsAg-oiNsC_K2bh0A1LUtJk8Om3vE2riAFG1JGEMdmqaBaxubyhXsz3_WmtZaC6W9RCipieZuqqGyZEg5Q4ElrxeZaOd15Jkxplfeab0M-VEkP4ksm7r-U9Ap6A7Jy7lQ0P2eK-jOFAWdtec4ZNFvJJ5HjWt-zkHLRHpIefjUcmR94Ev_8Ou3AJ1nzbotFXTF6sNycEq8VbVyZnwgp3cV-aPF3cN3AAAA___VI4f3). Today, the lanes carry traffic in only one direction at a time: north toward Washington in the morning and south in the evening. [_A two-way setup_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u2zAMBeCnkTcFEuOfaPDQxdvt2tGgJdomoEiBxNjN2xe-6BvclSAOznf-fM1fyJHT9hufNMqxzonOGkmEysyuo7-vQrVGTFTlHT6S39tOMxjotbXauBm98EFzi00YV2wJXUOjHVwLAMNgm32EAYN7QOg80QL3YfVojFn83fTO3sk3PF551hpnrYXO3lbo6LGaxfS-t2RItYYCSy432engsnFiXOMnH1RuPj-bOO4ir6ruvxRMCqbzPG9p8SfWndMmOV1fCqYLp2CK2WNUMEnBVF-5CArnpGBi7Tr936y_0drndwx6oeuMKVDQ8i6JguYkWYM-8aNgam3bP1yvYGrKGF4nx8i1H1Rrtidy_C4pP9z3GOFfAAAA__-fmZF3) would let drivers use them in either direction at any hour. The study, run with lanes operator Transurban, covers roughly 45 miles from the Springfield Interchange in Fairfax County south to Spotsylvania County. Fairfax officials [_have called the reversible design_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD3u4yAQxU-Du4mA4NgUFNu4-2-7pTWOB3u0BCwgJrn9KrnCdk960vv4_fmZf5ADx-03PsjV08-RWglUK-WZbU-vI1MpASOV-lzfNT23nWYt9Q2UAmlnvFc-aTbYrc6jIbQdOTVYo7UeBtXtzpphMeNI42iUGRdrxqsiXORyxaWXY9-x--QpJa1SSvfq4nVPo5eLvN1viiQJI2nlmvKl7nRy3jgy-vBOJ-XLPT264PZajyKuv4SehJ5aaxfvXzG1jy309CkQepL2o3uhJ4-cPb4gEK6UC-zpIP8MUFuChm9gsD3UFAJ8v8MRMMIdI3h-wcLbRqXCg0vFvwQc4UTYedsbvovQU5fdejQOgcttEEZuD-TwXVr_E_Lp9L8AAAD__yJrka0) one of the state’s biggest highway mistakes and are hopeful the plan can fix it. VDOT has stressed the project is in its early stages, with no construction timeline set.
## Tougher Driver License Rules on the Way
Starting Jan. 1, 2027, [_first-time Virginia drivers_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykUL1utTAUe5qwBeUcfgJDhm9hu9_aEaXkAEcK4TYJ0Pv2FVX7BB1ty5btt8f4sOw5LP_tRiaf8xjoSp5ypjhy39DnM1JK3gZK-XCvvB_LSiMqbCWAVP1op8wnjbUtnJltTbYvyIDua0TUGorV2A6cbjS4Dp1qFOm6qxS1rcNqrixCwebOA1A9AGAD5YwNdbN6V-3UAikStSLHeY9lXunkuHBgO_vXflIsp30rvFlzfiZR_RM4CByu6yqvyNMtChzuTQKHX6f8wa_9CIu07vA53Zx0kU-KSXqeKCSSkT4OjrRRyEmiQi1wKKJxz4u959RqUatls-y_S-Q__nca_AoAAP__cvqGjA) ages 18 to 20 must hold a learner’s permit for 90 days and complete a driver’s education course before they can get licensed. The change closes a gap in current law. [_Adults 18 and older_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAQhU-DOyyY4L-CIo27TZvSYvFgj8LaK5jF2dtHTrQnSPuNvtF77_MyXRxF2pYPd0PLJUwbHjkiM6aJhga_7wlzjm7DzI_5yftjWXECBa3UWqphcp6p4GRcNdvgDLqhQqu7wQBA1-lqtZ33Soe-V7q9Qh-MV7Np2tDPrQGltK_Inv-0VoPWGhpdB2iwD-qqWt9qVCiMwpl4TzWvWCgttJEL8bkXTLXfb1W0K_M9i7d3AaOA8TiO-nDleR4FjGcnAePL_CNyTlQwyUget4wyPSJmeVCMkt0XSgwBPUva5MuTmV1i2pYTgoJOwFglO99PiXLbCaOWm6P4m4n_OWex8BMAAP__oaKL1Q) can currently get a license by either holding a permit for 60 days or finishing a driver’s ed course, not both. Drivers 21 and older will keep that lighter standard. The new requirement applies only to the 18-to-20 group the state considers most inexperienced. Tougher Driver License Rules on the Way Starting Jan. 1, 2027, ages 18 to 20 must hold a learner’s permit for 90 days and complete a driver’s education course before they can get licensed. The change closes a gap in current law. can currently get a license by either holding a permit for 60 days or finishing a driver’s ed course, not both. Drivers 21 and older will keep that lighter standard. The new requirement applies only to the 18-to-20 group the state considers most inexperienced. White, speaking at a boxing event in London, England, said he was flying to Washington that night and . " We have a meeting on Monday, so sure, I'll have more to talk about after that," he said. Trump suggested White bring UFC fighters Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, and Amanda Nunes along as assistants. White posted an AI-generated image of himself behind the briefing room podium captioned, " On to the next chapter." The post has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left in October after five days on the job. The offer came a day after Trump named Stephen Miller chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Netanyahu Rival Tapped to Form Government Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday to form the next government, giving Benjamin Netanyahu's chief rival the first shot at ending his long hold on power. Eisenkot, a former military chief who leads the Yashar party, was of the 120-seat Knesset after the Oct. 27 election, against 46 for Netanyahu. He now has , with a possible 14-day extension. If he fails, Herzog can hand the mandate to someone else. On Gaza, Eisenkot is no dove. He , has pledged to dismantle Hamas's military wing within 18 months, and backs President Trump's Gaza plan, including an international force. His bloc remains divided over relying on Arab parties for a majority. SS United States Set to Sink Thursday The SS United States , the fastest ocean liner ever built, off Florida's Gulf Coast, where she will become the world's largest artificial reef, 57 years after her last voyage. Five city blocks long and 12 stories high, she set a transatlantic speed record on her 1952 maiden voyage that still stands, carried four presidents, and was built so the military could convert her into a troopship in under 24 hours. " It may not seem that way now, but back then she was the space shuttle of her age," said Susan Gibbs, whose grandfather designed her. The jet age retired her in 1969, and she spent nearly 30 years rusting at a Philadelphia pier before Okaloosa County bought her for $1 million. _Soon after its founding in 2013,[Mada Masr](https://substack.com/redirect/22a49fd0-d106-4ed6-b09f-c542b1f82dff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) emerged as the leading independent media outlet in Egypt and grew to become a pillar of independent journalism in the Arab world. As a dual-language Arabic and English publication, Mada Masr is read widely in Egypt and across the Middle East, as well as internationally._
_During one of the most tumultuous and consequential political periods in Egypt 's modern history, Mada Masr has proven to be an essential resource, providing drumbeat and critical coverage, mostly on Egypt--the largest country in the Middle East--but also on neighboring countries, including Sudan, Libya, and Palestine. It also continued to function at a time when Egypt's media landscape was censored and controlled to an unprecedented degree, both by direct repression--with Egypt becoming one of the worst jailers of journalists in the world--but also through acquisition, with Egypt's General Intelligence Service buying a spate of newspapers and TV channels to become the single largest media owner in the country. (The purchases were secretly made through a private equity firm, a story that Mada Masr broke.)_
_Over the years, Mada Masr has faced various forms of intimidation and harassment by Egyptian authorities: Its offices have been raided, its journalists arrested and interrogated, its foreign staff deported, and its website blocked for nearly a decade. And yet it has managed to survive and continue reporting._
_Two weeks ago, in an unprecedented escalation, Mada Masr co-founder and editor-in-chief Lina Attalah was put on trial on the charge of operating a website without a license. In a sham proceeding that only lasted a few hours and lacked any semblance of due process, a Cairo court swiftly convicted her, fined her the maximum 3 million Egyptian pounds (approximately $55,000), and ordered Mada Masr closed and its property confiscated. Nearly 140 rights organizations and media outlets, including Drop Site News, signed a[ statement](https://substack.com/redirect/53f83c1e-c459-4590-95df-771a95761be6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) condemning the ruling. Mada Masr appealed the decision with a court date set for November 25._
_Yet this week, Lina is once again being put on trial in a separate case on a similar charge of operating an unlicensed website, as well as an additional charge of publishing false news, for which she faces up to a year in prison. That trial begins on November 11._
_The op-ed by Lina below is being published exclusively in English by Drop Site News. She writes about the latest crackdown in Egypt, Mada Masr 's journalism, and operating within the political margins--as Egyptian authorities appear to be making a move to quash independent journalism in Egypt once and for all. _
_I worked at Mada Masr for four years, between 2018 and 2022, as a journalist and editor. During that time, Lina was arrested twice; global solidarity was crucial in helping to keep Mada Masr alive and Lina out of prison. Now, at this critical juncture for press freedom in Egypt, Mada Masr is once again calling for solidarity from their journalist colleagues around the world._
_-- Sharif Abdel Kouddous_

_By Lina Attalah_
CAIRO, Egypt--On October 27, I stood before a judge in a courtroom in Cairo with my defense team of eight committed lawyers beside me. A week earlier, I had been summoned for interrogation on charges of running a website without a license. It was the sixth time over the last few years that I had faced prosecutorial questioning. But it was the first time I was referred to court.
At the beginning of the court session, the judge repeatedly assured us that this was a small, simple case; it shouldn't be a big deal. Apparently for this judge, and for others with power, shutting down Egypt's leading independent newsroom was not a big deal. As the trial proceeded, all of our defense team's requests were summarily rejected, including requests for time to prepare a defense, submit additional documents, or to summon witnesses. As the space in the courtroom was being increasingly void of law, the judge decided to ignore all my lawyers and instead appointed a lawyer to take up my defense. I objected, my eight lawyers objected, and the judge proceeded to pronounce his ruling in this small, simple case, as I was being forcibly carried by policemen out of the courtroom. I didn't get to hear the verdict.
After seven hours in dark, musty custody, I learned from a paper that I had to sign to be released that the court ordered Mada Masr to be shut down and imposed a fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds. Just like that, 13 years of journalism practice had ended in a five-minute judicial performance.
That day in court came at the tail end of various other encounters with the law, where we took every initiative possible to avoid that outcome. A media law was passed in 2018 ordering us to get licensed. We applied right away but did not get a response. In 2020, when the legislation's bylaws were finally published, we applied again. Again, we did not get a response, despite the law obligating the licensing authority to provide a response within a 90-day period of the application. In 2022, we learned during an interrogation session at the public prosecutor's office that in fact, our license had been rejected, a decision that was never addressed to us and never included any reasoning. Nonetheless, we contested the decision at the State Council and when that contestation was rejected, we resubmitted our application with additional paperwork. We have received no response from authorities since 2023. Recounting these details is only an index for how we have always tried to stay within the bounds of a law designed to control, rather than to regulate.
Our battle has not just been to do independent journalism, but to institute in a sustainable way--including through legal practice--the expansion of the space allowed for us and others to operate.
* * *
In 2013, we, a group of journalists from Cairo, came together to create Mada Masr in a moment of political turmoil. Regime change was at the door, followed a year later by the election of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi. Thirteen years ensued of heavily tightened political rule with very little spaces of politics left, including power politics, and a rising integration in the global economy as one of many debt-drunk "emerging" markets, all in the midst of a radically shifting region.
That summer of 2013, the urge was to understand the moment, to give it shape in thinking and writing, to create a record of it. In doing so, we sought to keep people engaged in these transformations, and to find the connections between them and their daily lives. This is the space of politics we have been building over the last 13 years.
In our minds, journalism has always been a vocational space through which we can resist the active cancellation of politics. In times where this cancellation is manifested in the removal of spaces and people--unrepresentative parliaments, powerless opposition parties, fractured civil society, jailed regime opponents, propagandist media--independent journalism, with Mada Masr at the forefront of it in Egypt, kept some of this space alive. The substance of this space is asking questions, finding answers, thinking about them, and presenting all of it to the public, which enlarges the scope of the questions and the answers. It's the dynamism of thinking that keeps life political.
Keeping our life political, living our life politically, is a way to assert the legitimacy of our existence as a people; a legitimacy that transforms our need for dignified life into a right.
Over these past 13 years, we have been working, and over our heads, a chorus was repeating at Egyptians, at times shouting at us: that those in power know it all, that the stability of our country lies in their hands alone, that we should just mind our own business (business here is strictly tied to putting food on the table if you are from the middle class and below), that we are too needy, that many sacrifices are made for us. At Mada Masr, we simply chose to ignore the shouting, and do the work.
Today, it is not surprising to find ourselves being punished because we ignored the shouting. This is why we now find ourselves under a storm of targeted shouting.
And this is why we are fighting to expand that margin of space for us and others to operate. And this is why we still hold on to our right for appeal, with a court date set for November 25.
And this is how we will go back to court next week, on November 11. Because upon my release last week, I learned that I had been convicted in absentia in 2024 on charges of publishing "false" news and running a website without a license (again) and sentenced to one year imprisonment and (another) LE2 million fine. The ruling was handed down in absentia even though I always lived in the country. They had charged me and tried me and never told me. We will go back to court this week, and we will try to push for our defense statements to be made; this time adding that journalists should not be jailed, not only as a moral position, but also as a right inscribed in Egypt's constitution.
And because journalists should not be jailed, and because there is no individual salvation in a context like this, we hope to come out of this court session free, but also followed and preceded by another 26 journalists behind bars. The latest of these imprisonments are six young journalists, some of whom I have personally mentored, and together, they made up the entire newsroom of the fact-checking platform Matsadaash.
I hope to come out of court next week, and make it back to our newsroom, and stay there until the late hours of the day trying to understand, report, write, further institute, and have coffee with young journalists, including with those of Matsadaash, who made their entry into our world with the magical double "C": curiosity and courage. These are the substances of political living that we are fighting not to lose.
_Lina Attalah is the co-founder and editor-in-chief of Mada Masr. She lives in Cairo, Egypt. For press inquiries, contact mada@madamasr.com._

## Houston Limits Police Calls to ICE
Houston Mayor John Whitmire [signed an executive order](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD0O3CAUhE9jd1jw1j_rgiKNu02b0sLwMEQYLHi7eG8fOcoN0o5Go_m-X6_1pXzwcf-pDpR02bRGrCUgEeb1SIVOVBrtO1CqsdigirMhrcBhZEIwPq9Kk__gKlojN25m0aIU09wDDBPvWydHPQ0cez2OWhulxdDDNoO1ehwmsCBaL-81IfgsgItedA-jtufzOU8Am0Clmp6j8ZRyRw4JL1Vs-KYP5k6now3SEZ2lefxoYGlgqbV2Nl0wuvQulOJdamC5sRpY_oXsUN-U2e_kIqvO0-EzsuL3WBheqN83EkvZYGbBH5583Fl1GJk7DdMpktJUmNfYZmnO6kPwZZyanu-H8uHvL_pPnR8JfwIAAP__jGSPDQ) Friday that bars police from calling ICE during routine encounters, such as traffic stops, unless the person is arrested for a jailable offense. Whitmire, a Democrat, tied the move to Tuesday's elections, when Gina Hinojosa [ousted Gov. Greg Abbott](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2yozAQhE8DmSj98PgJFGxC9jbdkBqLkVFZaChpDPbtt_DuDV44Nd1fdfef7_kbQgzp_hs2tPzyNCc8S0RmzPNGhXcEh_4Zmc5UfISy-kizlroTSgk5zuA4HDirerE3uYyqRqv6sdX6q5dtvVozGpRDK1tjpOu_ZN-7znuPUi2qM2DqYC-aUnJUWqpWNWaB2zAMY6_1TSFA1UpcAlNueEXGFxQf33RgbhxtdbQr814q86vSU6Wn8zybRw6Fj-td6ekqVOnpYxT_j5WehSmJM8QoYtgCi-BQOKIdM3CgJEISGctOqaBgEgtu5DJwEQyPkO5ipxPzpfoH3uBNWRR4lzrbZb_AoXR91cr7BiF-ovIPFz6s_hsAAP__Yq6VUA) to become the first Democratic governor in more than 30 years. "_I've said many times, elections matter_ ," he said. In April, Whitmire pushed to amend a similar City Council ordinance after state leaders [threatened to withhold](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGSnDAQRU8jMk2pG3aAQIETsnXqkBKitWpboCmpd7Rzexcu32CzDl71-___el_fHSc-P366g6x8hbye1GoiESrrkas8yHkKn0lyO2tIrsaQ8ooG7xpAm3l1XvhJK3S73cw-Q0cWxnlAfBvN0EULQ2-2KezjRP22hx7MG7p-uM_Gm8lB37G9vgGYGdDAALd-d9s0TfOIuAE5pwZDO0suN4kk9OVqSK_8pHLz-eiSjSKPqvofCheFS2vt5hP7PxjzZ5V8XpTC5eqlcEnZu6RwuZwKFwCFi7mu_7Q-3CsX_TvHU7fIcnAhnfhJ-lGoVu3zGajQ6Uk3lqg9y0vnENizS5egK3Z_NE6J631Ug_k4HKd_SeWbAz8t_g0AAP__r4aRcg) more than $110 million in public safety funding. With Abbott in office until January, Whitmire said _, "I will take that risk and I know I'm doing right_." The Department of Homeland Security [criticized the order](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOiN78UEoXFxDl2uvRIu9BEuGRfYGkrf_lbzCX480M9_3_z7dMaa4P_7hRk5eC087XSWRCOVp4yIHoaflmYSvvSwJy7oknkBDp4xRepjQSzxpMnVwsw6DqcmZfrAAf3pt69URWA9I0OpgQ2eDNv3cdoO2fTsTWKyj-7QZowcD2ljTtAHn2-029ACzIcTKagpRODeyktALy5LefFJuPG91cqvIUar2bwVjBeN1Xc3Crw_GJ69gPDhFib5UMK78LMK72vDNWc2cpCjCnN4qelKe-aCMEnlXc3qSuvAk5TOWlYr6LtfZheOKKcXS9ZXVjw1j-v6QX-o7HfwEAAD__0j2iKg), saying, "_We remain disappointed that sanctuary politicians seek to limit cooperation with ICE_." A spokesperson added that seven of the 10 safest U.S. cities cooperate with the agency.
## Republican: Limit Hinojosa's Powers
Republican state Rep. Brian Harrison is urging Gov. Greg Abbott to call a special session to [curb the governor's emergency powers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OgzAQhJ8GOiPbOPwULq6hy7VXoo29BkuGRfYmJG9_4l7h6pFm5vt-7vMdYor78g0bWn4Hmnc8S0JmzPNGhQ8Eh-GZmM69hARlDYlmLXUnlBJynMFxfOGsam8f0o-qRqv60Wh966WpV-uddsNopDaAoKBrHQx9Z_o23Lq-Q6ijvdqUkqPSUhnVtB4ewzCMvdYPhQCVkegjU254RcY3lJA-9MLcONrqZFfmo1TtV6WnSk_neTaB3hfGlVd6OihFjq5UelKKV7HSM4uDTsziSPARDHlBLiLujra4L8LjJpZrYKcs1liYcnRioUN4DAhcZ-uPM6YUS9dXRi4bxPR3hv_p8GX1bwAAAP__-vGKTw) before Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa takes office in January. Harrison warned [in a letter to Abbott](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQhZ_GdCB7MD8uXGzjLttuiQY8gFcGIzwJydtfkVe45Uij75zv_HsMDwwx7Mtf3Mjye07DTleOxEznsKXMB-FE8zNyuvY8R8zrHNMAEtpSqVKaAScOLxpU4e0ovVEFWdUZDdB0UherbTqSdStx9n1rNNKkGwUeeqOxA6_bItibppQ0CqTSqqo9jn3fmw5gVIQotCQfOJ0Vr8T0xjzHT3rRWU1pK6JdmY8s6j8CnAB3XVf1zMjJ4-d-EOAyp_MjwN1q3xOZBLgvSoC74wU4pQQ42QhwS9ixXMOe_qeM5XLSUuI4JuaS3jQ9b9_ySBedApyBFpq6qaXsBLjitP64Qowht53QctkwxG9N_uW6Lws_AQAA__-__40z) that Hinojosa would inherit power to "modify laws, ignore laws, or create and enforce laws" on a whim. He said no governor, Republican or Democrat, should hold such authority under a 1975 disaster law. Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, [called Harrison's push "irresponsible"](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb9GMyxAn2hAsInZ23RDq9FG2UGx6J5h5u-33F942Q1unbr3_PmevyHEcG6_4UDLb5_mEwtFZMY8H4n4QljQPyOncpKPQLuPadZS90IpIccZFg4vnFW9WifXUdVolRk7rb-M7OrdKuO0bpUawHvXtu5Ld71Xq8HeQw_G1MHeNKXkqLRUnWraFdwwDKPR2ikEqDqJa-CUG96R8Q3k4ye9MDdLOupod-aLqvZXpadKT6WUxqd3d_-4C5We7ljpKeP1dDEscIoI5YAHZkHPbUNiEuBcYhbEOVxiu-lnyiTwwLzhuXzElQpmEg59yij2cKa_iUAwPJBE8j4sWGe7XiXEGKg3VSe3A0L8P5J_6PZl9b8AAAD___96lEc) and warned that after such an overwhelming vote, the move could hurt Republicans' reputation "for a generation." Harrison filed a bill to limit the powers in 2022, but it stalled. Longtime Texas political journalist Scott Braddock [called the session "highly unlikely"](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8GMyxonVEDgk3MZtMNLcBmpBbBgnaY9_evnHp_8KLu4Na5p-6_x_LQPvj4_Kt3VPR2aYlYS0AizMueCh2oLbozUKqxuKDL5kJaQMCdS8nFtGhL_oWLbFZlxDrJBpUcph7gNoi-2RQavAkYNcJk5IhoHEy67_BmremsxcariyalmCQI2cu2W7UZx3EaAIxErVkvcPWUcksbEr51ceErvTC3Nu1NUBvRUVj3h8HMYK61tjZ4-x-2dBZK8UoxmFe0vvgU-dXGYP45UjKYxfXZdIaVf_g843Ga4K2OhRfK_uBHqpi5y2nntCGPWHnweBJGHYk_L52YMoO5yWo9qg_Bl_vAevHctQ8fU_rlwC8F3wEAAP__OjiSkA) because Democrats could simply stay home and deny lawmakers the quorum they need to act. Abbott hasn't announced plans to call one.
## Texas' 10 Most Peaceful Small Towns
Dinosaur tracks, a 25-foot-deep spring-fed pool, and 70-foot sand dunes helped land 10 Texas communities on a list of [the state's most peaceful small towns](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGuqzAMxvGngS0oNmmBIcNd2HrXOyIDTolkSEV8m563P2ql8wRnt_7W7_t3m24UJR73v7Sz11dI08ElC6vyOe0p64Np4fBfNJUjB6G8BUkTWrwaAGOHiRaNT56gXv1s1wFq9tANDvHSWVdvHiB0DmdsbR_mMFhoHdNwCa5HDqvt6ujfNQA7AFpw0LQrzX3fDx3iDExUOctr1HQ2urHyi3KQr_Tks1nSXovfVB-5av9UOFY4llKakk5ZSYXy-6TCcYkaOVc4gjVvlflhmbyTiPnoTDzMJ99sukt9-vVRokjM165y9r5TlM9H_eVQT4_fAQAA__9SPn9o). Out west, Fort Davis is the state's highest town. Nearby, Balmorhea State Park has the world's largest spring-fed pool, which stays between 72 and 76 degrees year-round, while visitors in Monahans rent discs to sled down sand dunes. Southwest of Fort Worth, Glen Rose's Dinosaur Valley State Park preserves fossilized tracks along the Paluxy River. In Dublin, the plant that opened in 1891 as Dr Pepper's first bottler still makes cane-sugar sodas under its own label, around the corner from a Ben Hogan museum. East Texas picks include Crockett, gateway to a 160,000-acre national forest, and Kilgore, which lights its downtown oil derricks each Christmas. On the coast, Matagorda's west beach is reachable only by boat, kayak, or canoe.

name: Mary Peltola
subject: We’re in this for the long haul
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
I wanted you to get this update from me.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261109-1.yjYIa1&refcode=em20261109-4118&t=1&akid=4118%2E21716%2EaEyS7t)
I wanted you to get this update from me: **Ballots are still being counted, and right now, it’s still too close to call.**
We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is counted in this race for U.S. Senate in Alaska.
But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources that we don’t currently have.
As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain the top target of the DC establishment.
We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your help to fight back against their attacks.
It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to sustain our fight until every vote is counted.
From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days.
That’s why I have to ask:
[**If you can afford it today, please pitch in anything you can to my and Rep. Sarah McBride’s campaign at this critical moment. It all adds up to help us keep fighting.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261109-1.yjYIa1&refcode=em20261109-4118&t=2&akid=4118%2E21716%2EaEyS7t)

Thank you, and more soon.
Mary

Wall Street spent 2026 telling us the AI boom is a bubble. Amazon's stock lost $450 billion in market value sliding nine straight days after its February earnings. Analysts fret over the roughly $700 billion in combined capital expenditures the hyperscalers have forecast for this year alone.
Meanwhile, in one of the poorest states in the union, the money is actually arriving.
According to Governor Jeff Landry, Louisiana now has over $264 billion in announced investment -- the most of any state in America. A state better known for oil refineries, chemical plants and losing seasons is suddenly the epicenter of the largest private capital deployment in modern history.
Consider what has landed there in the span of about two years:...

name: Scott Colom HQ
subject: We’ll be blunt: We need your help in Mississippi
body:
Peter,
**Mississippi’s Senate race is too close to call, and we need your help protecting the will of the voters. Can you help make sure that we’re able to win the most closely divided U.S. Senate race in modern history?**
**[If you can afford it, we’re respectfully asking you to split $5 to Scott Colom and Wes Moore to help us make history in the Deep South.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261109-1.OFBGDy&refcode=em-20261109-1&t=1&akid=2286%2E1086043%2E12ht5l)**

We’re sorry to be so direct. But with the finish line in sight, we really need your help more than ever if we want to win.
Our team is working around the clock to protect the will of the voters. But it can take millions of dollars to make sure that this part of the process goes smoothly. And to be honest, we don’t have that type of money right now.
Every dollar we’ve raised, we spent to get us in this position. It was the right call, and the only reason we are on the verge of making history. But it means that we’re relying on this grassroots team to make sure we have the resources to finish the race.
**[Please, make a donation to Scott Colom’s legal fund and Wes Moore today. When the dust settles, this is going to be one of the most closely divided Senate races in modern history – so anything you can afford to give really makes a huge difference.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261109-1.OFBGDy&refcode=em-20261109-1&t=3&akid=2286%2E1086043%2E12ht5l)**

Hello, I hope this past weekend was great. I partied a little too hard but made some great memories. Thursday night, hundreds of people showed up for the latest [Offline](https://substack.com/redirect/124288f7-92ca-47c2-b71d-8df5e07e28a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) party in NYC. Friday I went to a charity event and afterparty and then Saturday a comedy show.
Last week, [Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/42fa01b8-eb9d-4593-be43-c43f48d00d52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) won 22 local races around the country, with another 12 still being counted. This brings the total number of Forward Party officials to around 110 and counting. We are winning races all over the place even while accepting that the majority of the candidates we endorsed wouldn't prevail because running as an Independent is very tough.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ed7cf29-348a-44cb-932d-1c7cac3824dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I feel for the candidates who fell short, as someone who has been on the losing end myself a time or two. You put yourself out there. You walk around your community, knock on doors, and shake hands for months on end. You ask your family and friends for support, which can be very uncomfortable. You take time away from your children if you have them, and put a lot of your relationships on hold even as you build new ones. You make a case you believe in. You open yourself up to judgment in the hope of making the world, or your corner of it, a better place.
And then you lose.
It makes you feel like nothing you do matters - didn't your neighbors or the voters see everything that you put out there? Does your heart and soul not matter?
I remember walking into that gymnasium in Des Moines, Iowa in February of 2020. I saw immediately it wasn't going to be our night. There was a small cluster of "Yang for President," and "Humanity First" signs and MATH hats among a sea of signs for some of the other candidates of that cycle, notably Bernie Sanders and Pete Buttigieg. We were going to have a very hard time getting above the 15% viability threshold in this precinct. My heart sank.
A very nice, well-intentioned Iowa mom grabbed me by the arm, looked me in the eye, and said to me with all the seriousness in the world, "Please, run again."
I nodded to her, thinking to myself, "Lady, I'm running right now!"
That night was the culmination of over 2 years of campaigning. After the campaign ended a couple weeks later in New Hampshire, I felt like a puppet whose strings had been cut. To say you're exhausted or wiped out doesn't quite capture it. It's like your spirit had been supercharged and then it left you for another host.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6d0e23c9-10f4-4411-978c-c668e8f1c5be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In that case, I didn't really have the chance to rest, as I flew out to Nevada to thank the team and staff there and then launched [Humanity Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/ba3a246a-57f1-41ae-a9e2-d1e35043bd6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to try to channel the energy of the campaign to change policy. It was only a couple months later when COVID hit that I really had a chance to recharge because the whole world shut down. I was secretly grateful.
Running for public office is incredibly taxing and difficult - I try to appreciate everyone who does it. And losing - which I've now done twice - is hard. Most of the setbacks we experience in life are not public; if you get laid off, for example, it's very bad but the person you pass on the street has no idea. When you lose a campaign, you feel like EVERYONE knows and regards you as a loser. Which technically, you are.
But in the big picture, though it might not feel like it for months afterwards, you've won. And that truth settles in over time.
You did something hard that others only think about doing.
You stood up for your beliefs in a way that reflected your values.
You impacted more people than you know. They admire you.
The folks in your life - the ones who really matter - will appreciate what you did. Forever.
You developed muscles, character, relationships and capacities that will serve you well in ways that you can't even anticipate.
Many people you don't think even noticed your campaign - who might not have voted - were moved by it.
And hey, the best part is that, afterwards, no matter what stress you're navigating, everything else feels easy in comparison. Until you decide to do it again. 
Thank you to the candidates, win or lose! Check out [Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/42fa01b8-eb9d-4593-be43-c43f48d00d52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) if this made you think about running. This week on the [podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/397bb4d3-4ed6-4be2-91da-a619be72dbc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) I unpack the blue wave Election Day returns and answer your questions with Zach Graumann. name: Scott Colom HQ
subject: We’ll be blunt: We need your help in Mississippi
body:
We’ll be
blunt:

Mississippi’s Senate race is too close to call, and we need your help
protecting the will of the voters. Can you help make sure that we’re able
to win one of the most closely divided U.S. Senate races in modern
history?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261109_1.2yiZBA&refcode=em20261109-1&t=1001&akid=9999%2E582294%2EE-wvZF ]If you can afford it, we’re respectfully asking you to split
$5 to Scott Colom and Chris Pappas to help us make history
in the Deep South.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261109_1.2yiZBA&amount=5&refcode=em20261109-1&t=1002&akid=9999%2E582294%2EE-wvZF ]Donate $5 »

We’re sorry to be so direct. But with the finish line in sight, we really
need your help more than ever if we want to win.

Our team is working around the clock to protect the will of the voters.
But it can take millions of dollars to make sure that this part of the
process goes smoothly. And to be honest, we don’t have that type of money
right now.

Every dollar we’ve raised, we spent to get us in this position. It was the
right call, and the only reason we are on the verge of making history. But
it means that we’re relying on this grassroots team to make sure we have
the resources to finish the race.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261109_1.2yiZBA&refcode=em20261109-1&t=1003&akid=9999%2E582294%2EE-wvZF ]Please, make a donation to Scott Colom’s legal fund and Chris Pappas
today. When the dust settles, this is going to be one of the most closely
divided Senate races in modern history — so anything you can afford to
give really makes a huge difference.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261109_1.2yiZBA&amount=5&refcode=em20261109-1&t=1022&akid=9999%2E582294%2EE-wvZF ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Scott Colom HQ

subject: The words that inspired Michelangelo
body:
Before Michelangelo painted “The Creation of Adam,” before Rembrandt painted “The Sacrifice of Isaac,” there were the words that inspired them...

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcmq3DAQRb9G3tlo8LjwIsTP0JDuDL3I0shStV3EGlDJ75G_Dx06P5BtneJUce_P63LVeKDfbtrBiESLDXbJO3yEZCnvOqOniAmsQ7PDIrlsSyFKPizaZHyHpdaFHRsp-kdfwCi6oZZyqGVb7KPuG3gYPlglhlVzDXxQ0ghYAVph1qbA8ekTgg9CcSW6qtW97IEbucrOwKNhNT-j1Rkq9IQWyIQQYzgwo6EqpK04xj3nSEx9YnJmciYwZ4Jqx-Mgqw-owJ5MzjZ4nYHJeQMPhFRSDul3acKZCEoTXNQegy_XEH4xNRNsDnz-HCwwNXHRNe2Ny1p-qa_T1-nt7c5ke2a3UDiTea7EFCiCyei3F3Jg8XRMTeA0Hq-h0S5q3DxT0-uRvwdfMPgMPjM1XW73b5cfb9PyvSsv93v5L6UijTZ-4HEgtR2r-fZUVya4Iv9vd--j_BMAAP__31Ws4w)
---
| | Dear Friend, Before Michelangelo painted “The Creation of Adam,” before Rembrandt painted “The Sacrifice of Isaac,” there were the words that inspired them... **The Book of Genesis.** For centuries, these opening chapters of Scripture have moved the greatest artists of Western Civilization to create some of the most iconic works ever made. Many of these masterpieces accompany the lectures in one of our most popular free online courses, “The Genesis Story.” **Now, I’m thrilled to introduce an extraordinary opportunity for you to bring them home.** We’ve compiled these paintings, along with many others featured in the course, into a one-of-a-kind coffee table book, **“The Genesis Story: Course Companion.” And I’d like you to receive a copy.** With this exclusive book, available only from Hillsdale College, you can read the very passages that led Michelangelo, Rembrandt, Gustave Doré, and other masters to create these incredible works of art, and see what those words became in their hands. And with these works all in one place, you and your family can enjoy page after page of divinely inspired art. **[You can reserve your copy of “The Genesis Story: Course Companion,”](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcmq3DAQRb9G3tlo8LjwIsTP0JDuDL3I0shStV3EGlDJ75G_Dx06P5BtneJUce_P63LVeKDfbtrBiESLDXbJO3yEZCnvOqOniAmsQ7PDIrlsSyFKPizaZHyHpdaFHRsp-kdfwCi6oZZyqGVb7KPuG3gYPlglhlVzDXxQ0ghYAVph1qbA8ekTgg9CcSW6qtW97IEbucrOwKNhNT-j1Rkq9IQWyIQQYzgwo6EqpK04xj3nSEx9YnJmciYwZ4Jqx-Mgqw-owJ5MzjZ4nYHJeQMPhFRSDul3acKZCEoTXNQegy_XEH4xNRNsDnz-HCwwNXHRNe2Ny1p-qa_T1-nt7c5ke2a3UDiTea7EFCiCyei3F3Jg8XRMTeA0Hq-h0S5q3DxT0-uRvwdfMPgMPjM1XW73b5cfb9PyvSsv93v5L6UijTZ-4HEgtR2r-fZUVya4Iv9vd--j_BMAAP__31Ws4w)** an exclusive hardcover book from Hillsdale College, for a generous donation of $100 or more by clicking the secure link below: [https://secure.hillsdale.edu/donate/genesis-story-course-companion-book](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcmq3DAQRb9G3tlo8LjwIsTP0JDuDL3I0shStV3EGlDJ75G_Dx06P5BtneJUce_P63LVeKDfbtrBiESLDXbJO3yEZCnvOqOniAmsQ7PDIrlsSyFKPizaZHyHpdaFHRsp-kdfwCi6oZZyqGVb7KPuG3gYPlglhlVzDXxQ0ghYAVph1qbA8ekTgg9CcSW6qtW97IEbucrOwKNhNT-j1Rkq9IQWyIQQYzgwo6EqpK04xj3nSEx9YnJmciYwZ4Jqx-Mgqw-owJ5MzjZ4nYHJeQMPhFRSDul3acKZCEoTXNQegy_XEH4xNRNsDnz-HCwwNXHRNe2Ny1p-qa_T1-nt7c5ke2a3UDiTea7EFCiCyei3F3Jg8XRMTeA0Hq-h0S5q3DxT0-uRvwdfMPgMPjM1XW73b5cfb9PyvSsv93v5L6UijTZ-4HEgtR2r-fZUVya4Iv9vd--j_BMAAP__31Ws4w) Thank you for your continued support and generosity. ## Storms Boost Reservoirs
Storms earlier this month [lifted](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE9jMiPbGAyBg03IZtMNUeNpDy01P7ItEHP6Fau9wZdVUHpVen9e0wuIafv8hhV9gW-cNrwyYymYpkLMK2yZ8QPhXvLBcO8xzmkyynRSa6mGCUKhEycL1ds3XRicrdBrN1hjhrYZqsU71fTaGZhbZRVE3TXB6lmH0CJC33cV-YentRp0o1pj69jOvZnnPmrn2t72wip8U9lTXRaERN99g8j3fmKqw75W7JdSjiyaX8KMwozXddXwjbAS309BmPFZEGbUWphRPWmhXPZEQf7nyQjMMgFtMhJzljkdMmHGdO6UsnRKmLFK_n1cxEy5c8KqzwrE_y6Un9o7vfkbAAD__1Zwg9o) Salt River Project's reservoir system from 53% full on Nov. 1 to 70% by Nov. 6, the utility said. The system gained about 120 billion gallons, with October and November bringing the Salt and Verde watersheds' highest inflows on record. Pat Tillman's legacy [continues](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkLuK7DAQRL_GzjxI7bYegYKbTDY33dC05NZYID-QxQyer1-87B9sWBRUcc7XY3xQyml9_qeFXaVPHFd-H5lr5TLWlPNC65H5SeGcjz3TucXoywgCVCdlJ-xIoaYXj0jt5HoVrMaWndQWAezQ23Z2xhqUYTIqeNVroKAHUohBCvSkNbTJXXtSCit7MQDe4uANeG-i1HowaBoUPKW6lVudmUr6bCvFfG4vLrewLW12c6370fT_Grg3cKf9oriqK5SaQuYG7jvV7pepiyaGwYIIli0KCahVjL32KqCVCNwWN-3vlHM6lG5QPBdK-ees_tXTy8F3AAAA___9X3rT) to inspire millions as Friday marked what would have been his 50th birthday. The Arizona State and Arizona Cardinals star joined the Army Rangers following the 9/11 attacks and was killed by friendly fire in Afghanistan in 2004. On Saturday, Arizona State's football team [wore](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupCAUhp8GOwwgihYU29jNtluaAx6U3aNMgB3jPP3N3Fe49Z_8X77vz2N5QKR4br_hQFvhHZYTr0JYK-alRqIDzkK4gb_38iS4UwguL0qogUvJxbSAr_GFi4Zmtd3gJ6MbtNJMWqmp76Zmt53vjHQduNV5CGoY3Cq1NM5MvRDjiE20nz8pxSQ70Svdht6NyrkxSGP6UY9MC1xjTbmtO0KO73RCoDu9MLc-HQ3ZvdZnYd0vpmam5uu62hI_E1NzOktkav6LueBdmJo_hkzNUnCHpfIL8R-XgvtEhBvykFJ1QMT_nzGkfJQm2_V5RaJYBsO02A6I9M2tP032suorAAD___algc8) white-gold-white uniforms with a "PT 42" helmet decal in honor of Tillman. Meanwhile, the Pat Tillman Foundation's scholars program now has [more than 1,000 members](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OrSAQx58GOwyMqFBQ3Mbu3HZLMyroJIgGyDGep9-42TfY7lfM_L--XuMLKVBc_-PubMGPH6O7cnCluDQWCmHHmINbcb63fAa8D--nNIKAjkvJhRlxLvR2o8JqsU03m15VzsreKADTNqbaLMgGJi-00UobJ5TAzvtJC2FmD1MHFdlHT0phZCNaULVvJw3TpL3s-1YrzZRwC5Uj1WVzmOhzRPThPt4u1fOxV8FupZyZNf8YDAyG67pq_HjcKdzPAYPhcWAwSMlgEA-dWPhvQZ4f4BTzSYniyncKgY6YOQC_HabM0ReX-EaZLw7LxtGvG0bKBSODoUp2Oa_nKXc9U2LdkcJPsvLXUd8WvgMAAP__pPiMdw), and the annual 4.2-mile Pat's Run draws about 30,000 people to Tempe.

Hello Friend, Spiritual strength doesn't come in a single moment. It's built over time. And after more than 40 years of pastoring and preaching God's Word, I've learned that consistent time in Scripture is the key to a grounded, courageous life of faith. That's why I created the brand-new _**[2027 Pathway to Victory Daily Devotional](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckc2OnDAMgJ8m3ED5I3QOHFrR6Wnb7WmPkUk8jCUgUWKo9u2raXdeYM_-Psuf_PbiX4BW2pefsOG4pJx9qR5uBeu9MhS-pfKejnID4jvtXkvtWqVaefEQmE70Fpo4WnDWOdfgqIaL1UYqJZv72Pda6QFUP4MMcZ6N7MMAMwxOzs5F09D4WKiUvCijevmls7feqn6eowEjnY3CSozEqXSP2wpWirgzwdqFtDXreGfOVZivQl-FvlYMR8Eu89mlsgh91VIPbeYzxnZZlDDXmo4S0IcUUZjp7fs3od3Bmw-wZaBlF2aKQOu7j3gmprTD-kH8N4WZckk1Y2Dal4_RhpGOTZgJN6AnH9LOuLMw0--h_fHr9bV9pjZljPkPrStVNwgrl4f1r4c_-4Fz1H8DAAD__89Fl8A),**_ a weekday guide to help you start each day with biblical truth and encouragement. Every devotional in this 260-entry collection was written to help you think biblically, live obediently, and trust God more fully. Whether you're struggling with uncertainty, carrying the weight of past mistakes, or simply seeking God's direction, this resource is designed to meet you right where you are. You'll begin the year by discovering how to embrace the new beginning God offers. You'll turn your attention to Jesus Christ through Holy Week and a study of the end times. You'll follow the early church and see how the Holy Spirit empowered believers to stand firm in their faith. And you'll close the year examining the attitudes that shape your life, learning to find contentment and experiencing the freedom of forgiveness. These are not abstract ideas. They are time-tested truths drawn from over four decades of biblical teaching to help you walk closely with Christ each day. This beautifully produced 532-page devotional features a velvet red leather cover, rich gold and brown foil accents, and larger, easy-to-read print, making it both a meaningful spiritual investment and a joy to use.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: We broke the Republican gerrymander in NC, but our work isn’t over yet.
body:
Help these Democrats get across the finish line.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1664&source=&t=1&akid=5345%2E124072%2EKXAhCt) | | | |
---
Peter,
The GOP thought they could redraw North Carolina’s maps and gerrymander their way to victory in the midterm elections, but **their plan backfired:** North Carolina Democrats held ALL four of our congressional seats and flipped FIVE more – with more races still too close to call.
We broke the Republican gerrymander.
We won in rural, historically GOP districts.
We showed that North Carolinians won’t be silenced.
**However, our work isn’t over yet. We must ensure every vote is counted in the remaining congressional races, and we need your help to get it done.**
My first race for Governor was decided by less than 1% of the vote – _following a recount_ – so believe me when I tell you: It’s critical that every North Carolinian’s voice is heard.
**_[I’m doing all that I can to help our candidates, and I’m asking you to join me in supporting the Recount Funds for Democrats Raymond Smith Jr. in the 3rd District and Chuck Hubbard in the 5th District. Will you split $5 between their campaigns to help them win?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20278?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1664&amount=5&t=8&akid=5345%2E124072%2EKXAhCt)_**

Thank you, Peter.

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

name: Enoch for Congress
subject: This race is too close to call!
body:
| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | Hello Peter,

I would like to sincerely thank every volunteer who knocked doors, held signs, stuffed envelopes and canvassing bags, wrote post cards, called and texted voters! We could not have had a close race without all of you! I would also like to thank the donors who believed in this race. My opponent raised and spent an estimated $1 million to our $50,000 from small donors throughout our district, yet we were able to effectively use our resources to strategically win half the votes. For that, we thank the voters, who simply believed in me and my vision for this country, and rolled up their sleeves to get it done. We spent every dime getting it done...I can’t honor you now, but I will certainly honor you once this race is called in our favor!
My race has not been called by the Board of Elections, and we are absolutely not conceding this election by preparing for a recount if the race is not called in my favor. For the past few days, me and our campaign team and volunteers have been crunching numbers, helping voters cure their ballots, and raising funds for a possible recount, so this race is certainly not over for us!
Recounts are expensive, and we must raise the money to get it done. It costs $80 per precinct to do a recount, and there are 1050 precincts in my district, and we only have a few days after the race is called to apply for the recount. In Ohio, you can choose to do a partial recount, so we are selecting several precincts that we want to target. The Election Truth Alliance announced the recount, however they are a nonprofit organization, so they can’t show partiality, so they had to post me and my opponent’s websites. So far, we have raised enough to do a recount on over 10% of the precincts, but we are still in need of donations to cover more. Our goal is to make sure every vote is counted!
I am not an election denier, like my opponent. That is why I never requested a recount in any of my previous elections, but unlike those elections, the district this time around is more balanced between rural and suburban voters, and more politically balanced. A lack of monetary resources made it difficult to reach many voters, however I have established name recognition and voters across the district have come to know me, and despite raising less than 5% of what my opponent raised, we were strategically able to secure half the votes. Additionally, we believe that votes should increase, and not decrease on election night, and the last votes to be counted were in Hamilton County, where we received the most votes, and where they stopped counting. The number of estimated outstanding and uncounted votes makes a recount extremely necessary. This race was extremely close within 4%, so we want to make sure that every single vote cast was fairly counted, and the will of the people ultimately prevails!
Although pollsters and the media denied the potential of this being a close race before and after the election, our team expected it to be close. We carefully micro-targeted our voters and counted our votes and secured those numbers by targeting 60,000 more votes than we believed we needed to win. There were 13,860 votes (4%) between me and my opponent when the Secretary of State stopped counting, yet there was still over an estimated 11,000 election night votes, and at least six precincts that remained uncounted at the time the race was called. Additionally, there were over 14,233 provisional ballots that remained uncounted, uncounted military ballots, and early and absentee provisionals that needed to be cured.
Additionally, the turnout was reportedly high in areas where many rural voters had expressed that they would be sitting this one out...and low in black communities in Ohio, even though we could visibly see that like the rest of the country turnout was at Presidential turnout levels in black communities. I visited the BOE for early voting and witnessed lines wrapped around the building. Despite what the turnout shows, Black people showed up for this election! We remain hopeful and hope you will too!If you are able, please consider donating a recount in one or 2 precincts. 1 precinct is $80, 2 precincts is $160.

We elected Deb Haaland — the first Native American woman ever elected governor, in the state that barred her people from voting until 1948. Congresswoman Sharice Davids was re-elected. clean_body: We can make this a clean sweep We can make this a clean sweep | ~~ | | Peter, FIRST, there was an idea most people called impossible: five Indigenous women on one November ballot — three running for top statewide offices — in a country where, eight years ago, the number of Native women who had ever served in Congress was zero. THEN came everything the GOP could throw at us. $17 million in attack money. The Vice President sent to Alaska twice, then Trump himself. A recruited celebrity candidate in Minnesota. A DOJ lawsuit to block certification before a single vote was cast, and a President declaring our candidate “shouldn’t be allowed to run.” NOW, we've elected Peggy Flanagan — the first Native American woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate, after a 237-year wait. We elected Deb Haaland — the first Native American woman ever elected governor, in the state that barred her people from voting until 1948. Congresswoman Sharice Davids was re-elected. Congresswoman-elect Claire Valdez, won with 83%. Four for four. Mary Peltola leads Alaska’s Senate race by roughly 600 votes, with ballots still arriving from the most remote communities in America and the count running to November 18. She’s in court demanding every rejected ballot be explained. The other side built a recount fund on Election Day and kept its appeal alive. The last seat of the most historic cycle Indian Country has ever seen is being decided ballot by ballot, this week, right now. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | ~~ We didn't come this far to watch the last one from the sidelines. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/0755fd1c-d6ee-426e-8c2f-2cc2ab01d9e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I sat down Tuesday night while the returns were still coming in, and I cried.
I thought, I did it. Then I corrected myself. No. We did it. We did it as a country.
America didn't fail a f"ing open-book test.
I'm so proud of the people who showed up. I was overwhelmed watching those results, and I'm getting choked up talking about it now. After everything we've been through, it felt good to see the country reject the MAGA agenda and a government that keeps failing the people it's supposed to serve.
Y'all, we deserve nice things.
Since January 7th, I've been fighting for accountability for what happened to me and my coworkers at the Capitol. I've taken loss after loss. I'm not going to go through all of them again here. You know.
But Tuesday night was the closest I've felt to vindication since January 6th.
I went to Arizona to campaign against Andy Biggs. I went to Wisconsin to speak out against Tom Tiffany and the election lies. I wanted people to understand why those races were personal to me, why I hold the people who spread that lie responsible for helping create what happened at the Capitol.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..sC3MXf-A3kdEFdtWUCqNpk7AUqQVStNu4vg7wYWzw6g?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=224164146)
Biggs lost. Tiffany lost. Katie Hobbs is going back to the governor's office in Arizona. David Crowley is going to be Wisconsin's next governor. Congratulations, Governor.
And Derrick Van Orden lost his seat to Rebecca Cooke.
To the people who kept pushing the big lie: I'm pushing a big middle finger right back. I'm glad you lost.
Thank you to the voters who made that happen. I got to do my part, but you all went out and voted. That's why we get to have this moment.
Watching Michigan was beautiful too. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is going to the United States Senate. I adore that man. He ran on making life better for everyday people, and I love seeing a Muslim man win that kind of trust.
We can want a better life for everybody. Your faith, your ethnicity, your sexuality shouldn't decide whether your government cares about you. Abdul believes that. Watching him win meant something to me.
And my friend Jocelyn Benson is going to be Michigan's next governor. There are so many people I want to congratulate that I'm not even going to try to name them all.
I do want Democrats to spend some time understanding why we won.
Are people tired of Donald Trump? Are they tired of everything costing too much? Do they believe we have ideas that will make their lives better? Are they sick of the corruption?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc5b0bb-bc81-45d0-a92f-619e26134ecb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I think it's all of the above. And we have a responsibility to deliver on what we promised. People need to afford groceries and pay their bills. We have to show them that voting for us makes a difference in their lives if we want to maintain this coalition and expand it.
There's a part of me that keeps thinking it didn't have to get this bad. We could have been spending this election expanding Kamala Harris's majority. Instead, we had to fight our way back from what happened in 2024.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..sC3MXf-A3kdEFdtWUCqNpk7AUqQVStNu4vg7wYWzw6g?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=224164146)
We do this in our own lives too. We put off going to the doctor until something's wrong. We wait for the car to start making a funny noise before we take it to the shop. I wish we didn't have to wait until everything was f'd up before we decided to change it.
But let me not be Debbie Downer. I'm proud of this country. I want us to enjoy what happened Tuesday. I've needed a night like that for a long time.
I also know a lot of you want to talk about what accountability looks like now. So do I.
I had the opportunity to ask Governor JB Pritzker, how do we get accountability, when so many Americans rejected it when they elected Donald president again? He said, we need to look at what this administration is doing right now and bring to light the crimes they are committing now.
I've spent years seeking accountability for January 6th. I want it. I'm never going to tell the people who want it that they don't matter. But Congress also has a job to investigate what's happening today. Follow the money. Get the records. Bring people in to testify and make the evidence public.
Jamie Raskin is poised to take the Judiciary Committee gavel when the new Congress begins in January. I can't wait to see what he does with it. I'm going to be paying attention.
Where investigations uncover evidence of crimes, Congress can make criminal referrals. That doesn't mean Todd Blanche will act on them. I don't expect the man who was Donald Trump's personal attorney to suddenly start holding him and his allies accountable.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/acf8c7a1-eb3d-4c1c-9d4b-96a218bab36d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congress still needs to investigate. The American people deserve to know what their government has been doing, and the evidence needs to be gathered whether this Justice Department wants to act on it or not.
I'm not willing to treat this Justice Department's refusal to act as the last word. Gather the evidence now. Make the referrals where the evidence supports them. A future Justice Department should be able to look at that evidence and make decisions based on the law, whoever is involved. I can't promise you when we'll get justice. I want us to do the work that gives us a chance to get it.
And yes, holding people accountable includes the Democrats we just elected.
I'm not sold on Chuck Schumer continuing as leader. The way he handled the shutdown fights and the fight over ACA subsidies disappointed me. I want leadership that will fight for the people who sent us here.
With Hakeem Jeffries, I'm cautiously optimistic. He deserves credit for keeping a party with a lot of different ideas together. That's hard. I look at the divisions in the Republican caucus and I appreciate that our leadership has been able to get people on the same page.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/91ea92f5-114b-422b-98b6-35373e458179?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But I'm going to judge the next Congress by the votes it takes and what it delivers. I want votes on Medicare for All and a livable wage. I want food assistance protected. I want Congress to work to end the war in Iran and stop military aid to Israel. Those are issues the progressive movement ran on and was widely supported by the voters.
And I don't like that Jeffries takes AIPAC money. That bothers me. I want him working to get big money out of politics and fighting to overturn Citizens United. People who showed up Tuesday deserve to see their priorities taken seriously.
Those conversations have to happen now, while members are deciding who will lead them. What are you going to fight for? What are you going to bring to a vote? I want us holding our own leaders' feet to the fire too.
We need turnout like Tuesday's in every election. I don't want us waiting until everything is terrible before we show up again.
I'm going to enjoy this win. God, it feels good. And I'm going to be watching what the people we elected do with it.
Harry
