clean_body: After years of fighting for accountability, Tuesday felt personal. Thank you for showing up. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more After years of fighting for accountability, Tuesday felt personal. Thank you for showing up. | | | Nov 9 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- I sat down Tuesday night while the returns were still coming in, and I cried. I thought, I did it. Then I corrected myself. No. We did it. We did it as a country. America didn't fail a f"ing open-book test. I'm so proud of the people who showed up. I was overwhelmed watching those results, and I'm getting choked up talking about it now. After everything we've been through, it felt good to see the country reject the MAGA agenda and a government that keeps failing the people it's supposed to serve. Y'all, we deserve nice things. Since January 7th, I've been fighting for accountability for what happened to me and my coworkers at the Capitol. I've taken loss after loss. I'm not going to go through all of them again here. You know. But Tuesday night was the closest I've felt to vindication since January 6th. I went to Arizona to campaign against Andy Biggs. I went to Wisconsin to speak out against Tom Tiffany and the election lies. I wanted people to understand why those races were personal to me, why I hold the people who spread that lie responsible for helping create what happened at the Capitol. Biggs lost. Tiffany lost. Katie Hobbs is going back to the governor's office in Arizona. David Crowley is going to be Wisconsin's next governor. Congratulations, Governor. And Derrick Van Orden lost his seat to Rebecca Cooke. To the people who kept pushing the big lie: I'm pushing a big middle finger right back. I'm glad you lost. Thank you to the voters who made that happen. I got to do my part, but you all went out and voted. That's why we get to have this moment. Watching Michigan was beautiful too. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is going to the United States Senate. I adore that man. He ran on making life better for everyday people, and I love seeing a Muslim man win that kind of trust. We can want a better life for everybody. Your faith, your ethnicity, your sexuality shouldn't decide whether your government cares about you. Abdul believes that. Watching him win meant something to me. And my friend Jocelyn Benson is going to be Michigan's next governor. There are so many people I want to congratulate that I'm not even going to try to name them all. I do want Democrats to spend some time understanding why we won. Are people tired of Donald Trump? Are they tired of everything costing too much? Do they believe we have ideas that will make their lives better? Are they sick of the corruption? | | ---|---|--- I think it's all of the above. And we have a responsibility to deliver on what we promised. People need to afford groceries and pay their bills. We have to show them that voting for us makes a difference in their lives if we want to maintain this coalition and expand it. There's a part of me that keeps thinking it didn't have to get this bad. We could have been spending this election expanding Kamala Harris's majority. Instead, we had to fight our way back from what happened in 2024. We do this in our own lives too. We put off going to the doctor until something's wrong. We wait for the car to start making a funny noise before we take it to the shop. I wish we didn't have to wait until everything was f'd up before we decided to change it. But let me not be Debbie Downer. I'm proud of this country. I want us to enjoy what happened Tuesday. I've needed a night like that for a long time. I also know a lot of you want to talk about what accountability looks like now. So do I. I had the opportunity to ask Governor JB Pritzker, how do we get accountability, when so many Americans rejected it when they elected Donald president again? He said, we need to look at what this administration is doing right now and bring to light the crimes they are committing now. I've spent years seeking accountability for January 6th. I want it. I'm never going to tell the people who want it that they don't matter. But Congress also has a job to investigate what's happening today. Follow the money. Get the records. Bring people in to testify and make the evidence public. Jamie Raskin is poised to take the Judiciary Committee gavel when the new Congress begins in January. I can't wait to see what he does with it. I'm going to be paying attention. Where investigations uncover evidence of crimes, Congress can make criminal referrals. That doesn't mean Todd Blanche will act on them. I don't expect the man who was Donald Trump's personal attorney to suddenly start holding him and his allies accountable. | | ---|---|--- Congress still needs to investigate. The American people deserve to know what their government has been doing, and the evidence needs to be gathered whether this Justice Department wants to act on it or not. I'm not willing to treat this Justice Department's refusal to act as the last word. Gather the evidence now. Make the referrals where the evidence supports them. A future Justice Department should be able to look at that evidence and make decisions based on the law, whoever is involved. I can't promise you when we'll get justice. I want us to do the work that gives us a chance to get it. And yes, holding people accountable includes the Democrats we just elected. I'm not sold on Chuck Schumer continuing as leader. The way he handled the shutdown fights and the fight over ACA subsidies disappointed me. I want leadership that will fight for the people who sent us here. With Hakeem Jeffries, I'm cautiously optimistic. He deserves credit for keeping a party with a lot of different ideas together. That's hard. I look at the divisions in the Republican caucus and I appreciate that our leadership has been able to get people on the same page. | | ---|---|--- But I'm going to judge the next Congress by the votes it takes and what it delivers. I want votes on Medicare for All and a livable wage. I want food assistance protected. I want Congress to work to end the war in Iran and stop military aid to Israel. Those are issues the progressive movement ran on and was widely supported by the voters. And I don't like that Jeffries takes AIPAC money. That bothers me. I want him working to get big money out of politics and fighting to overturn Citizens United. People who showed up Tuesday deserve to see their priorities taken seriously. Those conversations have to happen now, while members are deciding who will lead them. What are you going to fight for? What are you going to bring to a vote? I want us holding our own leaders' feet to the fire too. We need turnout like Tuesday's in every election. I don't want us waiting until everything is terrible before we show up again. I'm going to enjoy this win. God, it feels good. And I'm going to be watching what the people we elected do with it. Harry You're currently a free subscriber to . At the end of the day, every voice will be heard. And when they are, I believe that we will come out victorious in this election.
This process will take time and serious resources. clean_body: Two friends. Two razor-thin races. One chance to have their backs. | Two Senate seats are hanging by a thread, Fellow Conservative, and they belong to two of my friends. Dan Sullivan of Alaska and Cindy Hyde-Smith of Mississippi are each in a race that is still too close to call, with Democrats holding razor-thin leads while the count continues. I've served alongside them, I know how hard they fight for their states, and I'm not going to stand by while Democrats try to win their seats. This fight could go on for a while, and it takes real resources to win it. Democrats are prepared to fight for these RED seats. We need to be able to match their efforts. If we lose these two seats, taking back the Senate next cycle becomes even tougher. I know we’ve been asking a lot all cycle, so if $8 is more than you can do today, Thank you for joining me in having their backs. God Bless, Tim Sheehy | " "I SERVED AS A NAVY SEAL, BUILT ONE OF THE LARGEST AERIAL FIREFIGHTING COMPANIES IN AMERICA CREATING OVER 200 MONTANA JOBS, AND STARTED A VETERAN-LED CATTLE RANCHING AND FEEDING OPERATION. | | Last week's results were historic, and we all deserve to take time to celebrate. We put so much work into it. Knocking doors, making calls, showing up for candidates in every corner of the country. It's a big moment, and it's okay to feel good about it. But I also feel a little bit of tension because I keep coming back to a simple question: _why_ did we win? We didn't win because people suddenly fell in love with a party. We won because millions of American families are struggling right now. They're hurting from Trump's war and his tariffs that have driven up the cost of everything. They're hurting from the gutting of health care. Those results were a cry for help. **If we miss that, we squander this moment.** **So here is what I think comes next. And we focus on what we can do to tangibly help these families: lower costs, protect their healthcare, and make life more affordable.** Winning gave us an opportunity to lead. It's not a mandate to just feel good about ourselves. It's our responsibility now to deliver. name: Kailee Buller
subject: Peter, Thank YOU!
body:
This wasn’t the outcome we hoped for, but I’m proud of the fight we waged together. Onward!

| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter,
Thank you, Central New York. The results are in. It was not the outcome we hoped for, but I’m still taking in everything you did for this campaign. I’m grateful beyond what I can put into one email.
Eight months ago, no one thought this race was possible. We had no candidate. We needed someone who would fight. I answered the call. As a first-time candidate, we raised over $500,000 in eight months and knocked on thousands of doors.
I grew up in Auburn, the daughter of a corrections officer and a nurse. Like a lot of young people here, I had to leave to find a good job. I spent my career serving this country, most recently as Chief of Staff at the U.S. Department of Agriculture. I came home because I believe our kids shouldn’t have to make that same choice.
We gave a voice to the people who feel forgotten. People who work hard and watch their bills climb faster than their paychecks. People like my family.
Those problems didn’t go away because the race is over. The other side will continue to raise our taxes and our utility bills, and someone has to keep fighting it.
This is a rebuilding year for our party, and I plan to be part of the solution. The outcome of the election doesn’t change what drives me or my commitment to you or this community.
To my husband, Eric, who uprooted our lives so we could take this chance. To our kids, who put up with a lot of long car rides. To our campaign team, every volunteer, and every donor: we learned together and fought together. To our Founding Members who joined at the very beginning: you were the heart of this campaign. I will always be grateful for the trust you placed in me and the honor of fighting alongside you. Thank you.
While this campaign has ended, I’m not done. Thank you for your faith. The fight continues. Onward!
With immense admiration and gratitude,Kailee Buller

name: David Hogg
subject: In the quiet moments
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Protecting the Democratic majorities we just won starts with the work we do right now.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261109-1&t=1&akid=4238%2E587540%2En8n1BX)
**I know we just wrapped the midterms, Peter, but I have to be real with you — we’re already laying the groundwork for 2028.**
The incredible wins we saw on Election Night weren’t happy accidents or guarantees. They were the result of our year-round candidate recruitment operation, on the ground campaigning and coalition building, early investments in critical races, and daily campaign advising. See, our power isn’t just built in the handful of months before a major Election Day. _It’s built in the quiet moments in between_.
The first 6 months after an election are always the hardest to get through. People think the work has stopped, so donations dry up fast. But for Leaders We Deserve, our most critical work starts right now, as we recruit candidates across the country and lay the groundwork for 2027 and 2028.
Holding the state legislative chambers we just flipped and protecting the Democratic governing majorities in the House and Senate starts with the work we do _right now_.
That’s how our slate of young, progressive candidates won last week — so we’re getting right back to work.
Over the next few months, we’re going to find the next class of bold, progressive young leaders. Organizers, teachers, nurses, and workers ready to fight for their communities. We’re going to invest in them early, support their campaigns, and stand with them all the way to the next Election Day. And we’re going to have the backs of every leader we just elected as they show this country what a new kind of politics looks like.
To do all of that, we need the resources in place to plan ahead. And the best way to do that is with support we know we can count on every single month.
**That’s why I’m asking you to lock in a monthly donation of $5 today.**
Monthly sustainers are the backbone of our organization. They’re the reason we can say yes to a promising first-time candidate, months before anyone else is paying attention, and help them build a strong foundation early. That’s going to help us win big in 2028, just like we did this year.
**[So Peter, will you start a monthly gift today? Even $5 a month adds up quickly and will help us prepare for the fights ahead.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261109_1_ask.TGQ9br&refcode=em20261109-4238&t=2&akid=4238%2E587540%2En8n1BX)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

**Election Night results are not final results.** Mail-in ballots, provisional ballots, and votes from military and overseas Americans can take additional time to count. **Every eligible vote matters, regardless of when it's counted.**

Politicians don't get to declare themselves the winners by throwing out votes they don't like. That's election sabotage, and it threatens to take the power to choose our leaders away from the people.

Congress must monitor federal election counting, investigate interference, and demand enforcement of voting rights protections. And **our representatives must prepare to act wherever credible threats to lawful vote counting emerge**.

# Iran
* **U.S. forces again target Qeshm Island:** U.S. forces fired "projectiles" towards Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday night, causing at least four explosions, Iranian state media said.
* Iranian officials said U.S. forces targeted several areas outside residential and commercial zones on Qeshm. "No damage was caused to the island's vital and service infrastructure," Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Hormozgan province, told state broadcaster IRIB.
* Residents on Qeshm Island reported hearing several explosions late Sunday evening, Iranian state media reported.
* **U.S. strikes affecting availability of essential medicines:** Recent U.S. strikes have damaged 15 drug-manufacturing companies and eight distribution firms, Iran's Food and Drug Administration said.
* As a result of the attacks, Iran is facing difficulties in providing 37 out of some 700 types of essential medicine, an agency's spokesperson told the Tasnim news agency.
* **Mojtaba Khamenei urges resolution on stalemate:** Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued new directives on ending the state of "neither war nor peace" with the U.S., Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said.
* "The supreme leader ordered us to end the no-war, no-peace situation," he said on Monday, according to Iranian media reports.
* Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged Washington to accept Tehran's two-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and said there have been no changes in Iran's position.
* "American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own. Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results. Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell," Araghchi [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/c57517c2-ae61-4e39-9ffa-4eec1aad85ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X.
* **Trump says renewed attack on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks progress:** President Donald Trump told CNN in a phone interview that as long as Washington sees progress in negotiations with Tehran it is "highly unlikely it's going to be necessary" to resume strikes.
* Trump nevertheless added that the U.S. had identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, that it would strike if military action resumes.
* The prime minister of Qatar, which has helped lead mediation efforts to end the war, arrived in Washington, DC, on Monday to meet Trump and Vice President JD Vance.
* **Iran hangs three men in connection with anti-government protests:** In Karaj on Sunday, Iran hanged three men convicted on charges related to nationwide anti-government protests in January, state TV reported.
* The three were convicted of armed riot, damage to public properties, and cooperation with Israel and the United States during the demonstrations. Iran has hanged more than two dozen people on similar charges this year alone.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed three Palestinians--two in new attacks and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and injured 15 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,643 killed and 175,962 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,613 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,833, while 849 bodies have been recovered.
* **Five Palestinians killed amid heavy rains:** On Sunday, at least five Palestinians, including four children, were killed in Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, after a sand cliff collapsed onto makeshift tents where displaced families were sheltering, Al Jazeera reported. The sand cliff collapse was triggered by heavy winter rains.
* An unknown number of people are reportedly still missing under the massive pile of sand and rock. Civil defense workers and nearby residents searched through the rubble, largely working with their bare hands.
* "This is a scene that should shame the conscience of humanity," the Gaza Government Media Office said in a statement on Monday.
* **70,000 tents flood as winter storm hits Gaza:** Around 70,000 tents were flooded within 12 hours when the first winter storm of the season hit Gaza this weekend, according to Gaza's Government Media Office. Civil Defense received over 2,100 distress calls and declared a maximum state of emergency.
* Dozens of displacement encampments--tents, shelters, and entire residential areas--were flooded by the heavy rains, Civil Defense said. In some areas, water levels rose 1.5 meters.
* In a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/a3d31771-9706-4497-ba99-ab13db36ed90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Save the Children said, "This is not simply the result of bad weather. Tents, shelter kits and fuel are waiting at Gaza's borders while children sleep in floodwater, because the Israeli authorities are blocking their entry. This is a choice, and children are paying the price. More than a year into the so-called ceasefire, it has failed to protect Palestinian children."
* **Transport companies announce suspension of services:** The Ministry of Health in Gaza said on Sunday it has received reports from a number of approved transport companies announcing the complete suspension of services. The companies attributed the decision to the accumulation of non-payment of their dues, and a large number of vehicles being put out of service due to frequent breakdowns, and an acute shortage of spare parts, oils, and tires.
* The Health Ministry warned of "serious and unprecedented repercussions that threaten the work of hospitals and primary health care centers."
* **80% of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli prisons infected with scabies:** About 80% of Palestinians detained in Israeli prisons, including women and children, are infected with scabies, the Palestinian Prisoner's Society (PPS) [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/b0626a91-fa5e-4698-9d08-3699fb974bf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday. Israeli authorities routinely deny adequate treatment, clothing, and hygiene facilities to Palestinian prisoners.
* Based on lawyers' visits throughout October and early November, PPS also documented violent raids every two to three days in some prison sections, with prisoners subjected to severe beatings, attacks by police dogs, rubber-coated bullets and gas. They also found systematic food deprivation, with prisoners receiving severely inadequate quantities and quality of food, and severe overcrowding, with prisoner forced to sleep on floors while guards confiscate mattresses during the day.
* **Herzog taps Eisenkot to form new Israeli government:** Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday formally gave Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a new government. Eisenkot now has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension from the president. If he is unable to form a government, Netanyahu could then be given a chance to put together a coalition. If Netanyahu is also unable to do so, new elections could be called.
* Eisenkot has said that parties can join his coalition if they agree to four conditions: recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; a duty of national service for all; recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organization; and a commitment to destroying Hamas's military and governing capacity.
* Netanyahu's Likud Party won the most seats of any single party, while his wider coalition won 53 seats, short of a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat parliament. Eisenkot's Yashar party emerged as the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, won a total of 48 seats. Two parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel won an unprecedented 19 seats.
* Israel's new members of Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday evening. Netanyahu and his cabinet will remain in office in a caretaker capacity, with limited powers, until a new ruling coalition is formed.

# Yemen
* **At least 44 killed in Saudi strikes on Yemeni village:** Airstrikes blamed on Saudi Arabia that hit homes in a Yemeni village near the capital of Sana'a killed at least 44 people, including 21 children, the Health Ministry in Sana'a said on Sunday. It was one of the deadliest attacks in the latest phase of the war, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/580339f5-a091-4d0a-807d-9d431fb441d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Associated Press.
* The strikes on the village of al-Shariya, east of the capital, also wounded 40 people, including eight children and nine women, the Health Ministry said. Rescue teams are still searching for missing people, and the death toll could rise.
* At least 91 airstrikes targeted six Yemeni governorates in the 24 hours from Saturday to Sunday, Ansarallah military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/f60bb347-d1ce-4db8-84cc-aeedcdd74b27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday. He added that the total number of Saudi-led coalition attacks since the latest escalation in the war in September was at 4,460.
* **Aramco headquarters damaged in Riyadh:** Several floors of Saudi oil giant Aramco's corporate office in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, were damaged on Sunday in what the energy ministry said was debris from an attempt to attack the building, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/c2cf49d9-53d9-406f-b8e1-bd48163f263e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Reuters.
* Ansrallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree [said](https://substack.com/redirect/175132b3-f131-4687-b661-c117a2030860?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday that Ansarallah had hit Riyadh's financial district, where Aramco's headquarters is located, and other targets in response to recent Saudi attacks that have killed and injured dozens of people.

# U.S. News
* **Trump diagnoses midterms loss, talks future immigration deal with Democrats on 60 Minutes:** In an interview with 60 Minutes' **Ross Douthat** on Sunday, President Trump [discussed](https://substack.com/redirect/d4927bea-1b96-453b-ad03-4993e7908563?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his party's historic midterm loss earlier in the week. In part, he attributed the loss to the Iran War, saying that voters "didn't like the war." "They didn't like the fact that gasoline went up," he said, while noting what he called the "great dislike...for Israel." In reference to a post-mortem from Vice President **JD Vance** posted on X last week, which singled out the Iran war, Trump said he would have made the same decision again, though he said he would have made the same post in Vance's position, and that he "liked" Vance's comments.
* Trump [acknowledged](https://substack.com/redirect/3eda7f96-4618-466e-8623-30e9d6b45565?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that his immigration-enforcement policy was "too tough" and likely cost his party in the midterms. He said he was open to a comprehensive immigration-reform deal that would secure the border, while allowing some immigrant workers to remain in the U.S. if they do not have a criminal record and have been living in the country for some time.
* **And yet: Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff:** On Friday, Trump [announced that](https://substack.com/redirect/2eb16b22-e6ef-4434-aaa3-3713b87a2695?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Miller** , previously his homeland security adviser and deputy chief of staff, will replace **Susie Wiles** as the White House chief of staff. In a Truth Social post, Trump said that Miller "gets it very good politically" and is a "great manager." Wiles likely wouldn't have been ousted if Republicans had performed better in the midterm elections, one source told Politico. And another source said that Trump was frustrated that she has acted as a "restraining bull." Miller, 41, has been a key adviser to Trump over both of his presidential terms and is the principal architect of Trump's hardline immigration policy.
* **Clean energy bill moves toward passage:** The Senate has released a so-called manager's amendment of a permitting-reform bill called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). The new version of the bill primarily seeks to address concerns around tribal rights. The clean-energy industry solidly supports BAAJA, though some environmental groups whose focus is blocking energy projects continue to object to it.
* The bill has the backing of Environment and Public Works Chair **Shelley Moore Capito** (R-W.Va.) and Ranking Member Sen. **Sheldon Whitehouse** (D-R.I.), as well as Energy and Natural Resources Chair Sen. **Mike Lee** (R-Utah) and Ranking Member **Martin Heinrich** (D-N.M.). Backers of the bill are optimistic that it could pass within the next two weeks, and they worry that pushing it to the next session would doom it.
* The argument against the environmentalist objections is straightforward: Efforts to transition away from fossil fuels and toward clean energy by relying on litigation and regulation will backfire politically if those efforts drive up the costs of energy, as the midterms just demonstrated. Only by allowing clean energy to outbuild dirty energy can the transition be made feasible. That requires beating back some of the powerful community groups that have been able to block clean energy projects.
* The advocates further argue that the current laws obviously do not prevent the fossil-fuel industry from building dirty-energy infrastructure.
* **Trump orders DOJ investigation of Democratic lawmakers:** On Saturday, President Trump said that he ordered the Justice Department to look into "criminal acts" by Democratic lawmakers. In a Truth Social post, he said that Democrats' threats of investigations and impeachment are "extortion at the highest level." He singled out Sen. **Elissa Slotkin** (D-Mich.), accusing her of threatening young conservatives. and said that "imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS." During an appearance on CNN's "State of the Union" on Sunday, Attorney General **Todd Blanche** [acknowledged](https://substack.com/redirect/455f5d36-fe4b-4f22-98a6-c5415b8f846f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Congress' oversight authority, but said that Democrats' rhetoric crossed a line. He refused to rule out the possibility that the DOJ would prosecute Democratic lawmakers for trying to investigate the Trump administration. Blanche said, "I would be very worried if I was a member" of the Oversight Committee. He added that the DOJ will provide legal defense to Trump officials facing scrutiny from Democrats.
* **In Alaska Senate race, Peltola leads by "a couple of hundred votes": **Alaska Governor **Mike Dunleavy** [told](https://substack.com/redirect/f2b813ec-b5d9-4adc-9c70-67d4d9274e99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a local radio station on Sunday that the state's Senate race remains "very close," with Democrat **Mary Peltola** up by roughly "a couple of hundred votes." Seventy percent of the votes are counted in the first round, after which ranked-choice voting preferences kick in. Further votes will be counted over the next two weeks. According to Decision Desk HQ, Peltola is barely leading Sen. **Dan Sullivan**. She has won about 48.2% of votes, and Sen. Sullivan has won 47.9%.
* Separately on Friday, Mary Peltola's campaign [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/378ceecd-dd19-4437-8a5e-90f0f78964a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it is suing the state to obtain access to records for absentee ballots that were rejected by Alaska's Division of Elections. The campaign claims that it sought access to the ballots multiple times but was denied, and that access is necessary to "ensure voters' lawful votes were properly counted." The state responded to the lawsuit in a press release on Friday, saying it was not constitutionally obligated to provide the information "in the manner requested by the campaign."
* **House Republican leaders expect impeachment of War Secretary Pete Hegseth:** House GOP leadership [expects](https://substack.com/redirect/475b959c-a752-4bc6-ab71-1cc7ca0a4b35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Republican defections to enable the impeachment of War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** , Axios reported. Outgoing Republicans have little to lose, and there is considerable animosity for Hegseth. Rep. **Don Bacon** , a retiring Republican from Nebraska, told Fox News that Hegseth didn't "have a lot of love" on the Hill. Rep. **Thomas Massie** plans to force an impeachment vote this week, accusing Hegseth of defying Congress, and of illegally continuing the Iran war. Hegseth has called the planned impeachment effort a "sham." Hegseth's removal by impeachment would require 67 votes in favor in the Senate.
* **Chuck Schumer says he has enough Democratic support to become majority leader; Chris Van Hollen opens door to a challenge:** Aides to Senate Minority Leader **Chuck Schumer** (D-N.Y.) [told](https://substack.com/redirect/0d633f41-16f9-42ab-923e-df3a2bf68678?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the New York Times on Saturday that the 75-year-old has secured commitments from enough senators to win another term as leader of the Democratic Party's Senate Caucus. Schumer has served in that capacity since 2017, and previously served as Majority Leader from 2021 to 2025. The announcement follows a push to change the party's Senate leadership, with a movement underway to draft Maryland Sen. **Chris Van Hollen,** Politico Playbook reported on Monday. Von Hollen had previously declined to challenge Schumer, hinting at a presidential run instead, [but a Van Hollen adviser said](https://substack.com/redirect/bb3e377a-4fb9-4f9c-9c68-5cbed275fd31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he had "received an outpouring of calls and is now in active listening mode. The door is not shut." About a third of Democratic voters view Schumer favorably, according to a May poll from New York Times/Siena.
* **ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at scheduled immigration appointment:** ICE [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/bbc7ff4a-ce46-4d99-806a-92350ea4b911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an 8-year-old boy as he was arriving at a scheduled immigration appointment in San Diego, Calif., last week, KPBS reported. A volunteer court observer filmed the incident, and said that she had "never watched a child by himself get detained in that manner." The boy, originally from Haiti, has lived in San Diego with his uncle since his father was deported in March 2025. The Department of Homeland Security says that his uncle lacked legal custody, so the boy was treated as an unaccompanied minor and taken into the custody of the Office of Refugee Resettlement "out of an abundance of caution." The San Diego Unified School district and other local officials demanded the boy's release to his uncle in a letter to DHS Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** and Health and Human Services Secretary **Robert F. Kennedy Jr.**
* **U.S. deportation flight of Iranians abruptly canceled:** At least eight Iranians were loaded onto a plane in Mesa, Ariz., in a deportation flight bound for Pakistan, before the flight was abruptly canceled, **Ali Rahnama** , a lawyer for the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/75c911f0-6b84-48cb-8333-4be5aa0f7841?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The administration said as recently as mid-October that it planned to deport Iranians to Iran through a third country, according to unsealed court documents.
* **Trump admin officials reportedly aware of Nvidia CEO 's affair with Chinese spy:** Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** [oversaw](https://substack.com/redirect/4614ff7b-32f7-4ee8-8e32-faf2cbf9d119?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the drafting of a classified memo warning administration officials that Nvidia CEO **Jensen Huang** had a close relationship with a Chinese spy, the New York Times reported. The memo, circulated this spring ahead of Trump's trip to China in May, drew on electronic surveillance of **Alice Huang** (no relation to Jensen Huang), a Chinese citizen and senior executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which bought about $2 billion in Nvidia chips and is suspected of helping smuggle restricted chips into China. U.S. officials concluded that Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. On Sunday, Nvidia opened an investigation in Huang after he acknowledged he had been intimate with her, with the company saying that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." Trump was briefed on the matter about a year ago and took no action.

# Other International News
* **Attack on gas field causes widespread power outages in Iraq 's Kurdish region: **An attack on the Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq's Kurdish region was targeted by a drone attack late on Sunday, taking the facility offline and causing widespread power outages, the AP reported.
* No casualties were announced, and the extent of the damage was not immediately clear. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.
* **Sudanese Armed Forces advances against Rapid Support Forces in West Kordofan:** On Sunday, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and its allies [fought](https://substack.com/redirect/7a0980f7-77fa-45e6-a72e-10f1bc4ee128?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) heavy battles with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Abu Minaiqir, about 34 miles north of El-Khuwei in West Kordofan, the Sudan Tribune reported. The SAF also said that it shot down a long-range drone near Wad Banda, its third interception in Kordofan in 72 hours, as it pushes west to secure routes for future operations in Darfur.
* **SAF detains Bashir-era official wanted by International Criminal Court:** The SAF [said](https://substack.com/redirect/068b317e-c35a-426f-9d18-e5196d17d050?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday that it had detained Ahmed Haroun, chair of former President Omar al-Bashir's National Congress Party, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes and genocide in Darfur in the early 2000s, Reuters reported. It was unclear why the SAF moved against Haroun, whose Islamist movement has fought alongside it against the RSF.
* **Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34:** On Saturday, at least 34 people died when a wooden pirogue carrying migrants and refugees [capsized](https://substack.com/redirect/5aa1a5ce-e062-42a3-9816-1fbda83d6a98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) off the Loumpoul dunes in Senegal's Kebemer department, between Dakar and Saint-Louis. The Interior Ministry said that one person was rescued.
* **Bangladeshi ex-PM Sheikh Hasina, who fled country in disgrace after repressing protesters, requests new passport to return:** On Monday, former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina [asked](https://substack.com/redirect/19a737fc-7f9b-4e86-8782-a972950feae6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Bangladesh's embassy in New Delhi to issue her a new passport and national identity card, Reuters reported. It is the clearest indication yet that she plans to return to Bangladesh, where she would almost certainly surrender before a court. As prime minister, she ordered a deadly crackdown on 2024 student-led protests, and last year a Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in absentia for her role in the repression. During the protests, Hasina resigned as prime minister and fled to India.
* **Drone attack on Colombian military base kills three soldiers:** A drone strike on a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, in northern Colombia, [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/b3508603-0b19-4dfd-a2d3-a2df4ef2853c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three soldiers and wounded at least 16 other soldiers, the Colombian armed forces said on Saturday. Colombian officials [blamed](https://substack.com/redirect/45635de2-dfa3-4414-b7e2-80b8b2277291?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the National Liberation Army for the attack. The drone strike follows a strike on the group inside Venezuelan territory last month. It is the latest in a wave of attacks on security forces since conservative President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August. Since assuming power, de la Espriella has canceled peace talks and escalated military operations against armed groups.
* **Guatemalan lawmaker, three police officers killed in attack:** Gunmen [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/f865729d-af46-4489-a058-6213ec529389?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Guatemalan congressman Julio Cesar Portillo Paz, of the right-wing National Unity of Hope Party, and three National Civil Police officers in an attack in Rio Hondo, Zacapa, on Friday, Reuters reported. President Bernardo Arevalo ordered security forces to assist prosecutors in identifying those responsible. The killings come three weeks after former anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa was shot dead in Guatemala City, fueling fears of a new wave of political assassinations.
* **Mexico arrests alleged Jalisco cartel leader linked to 19 killings:** Mexican forces [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/7853e695-83e2-435f-b29c-9bbd011a7e6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Rafael Álvarez, the alleged head of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel's "Los Rs" cell, along with 19 others in an operation in Zapopan on Sunday. The operation relied on intelligence from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, the Mexican Navy said. Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said that Álvarez, who was wounded in a shootout during the arrest and faces a U.S. extradition warrant, is linked to at least 19 killings, including last year's murder of Carlos Manzo, the mayor of Uruapan, in Michoacan.
* **Russian strikes cause power outages for hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians:** Russian strikes on energy facilities have caused power outages for more than 600,000 people in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region and 250,000 in the Kharkiv, Ukrainian officials and energy company DTEK [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e849cb9a-3552-4d20-a3dc-b6a55da4651a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The strikes followed a huge Russian assault on Saturday that cut power in five regions, which President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said was aimed at pressuring Kyiv ahead of U.S.-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi this week.
* **Poland opens terrorism investigation after gunman kills six in Krakow:** The National Prosecutor's Office announced that it is investigating the deadly Krakow shooting as a terrorist attack. On Saturday, a 24-year-old Polish gunman opened fire in Krakow's historic city center, killing six people, including a British national, and wounding 15 others. After the attack, police found the bodies of the suspect's parents and sister at his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski. He was wounded in a gunfight with police, and died of his wounds on Monday.
* **200,000+ people march in Amsterdam demanding action against Israel:** On Sunday, more than 200,000 people marched through Amsterdam in a protest [calling](https://substack.com/redirect/03c70851-08ed-4c5a-b4a5-8ccec12f2593?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the Dutch government to halt all arms sales to Israel and to tighten trade restrictions with the country over its genocidal war on Gaza. Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who participated in the march last year but was not present on Sunday, defended his government's record on Gaza, saying that it was exerting "greater political and diplomatic pressure" on Israel.

Drop Site Daily: November 9, 2026 | | | Nov 9 | | | | | | | | | | | | Palestinians at a tent camp in Gaza on November 7, 2026. Photo by Majdi Fathi/NurPhoto via Getty Images. Monday, November 9, 2026 - Iran: U.S. forces again target Qeshm Island. U.S. strikes affecting availability of essential medicines. Mojtaba Khamenei urges resolution on stalemate. Trump says renewed attack on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks progress. Iran hangs three men in connection with anti-government protests. Palestine: Killed and wounded in Gaza. Five Palestinians killed amid heavy rains. 70,000 tents flood as winter storm hits Gaza. Transport companies announce suspension of services. 80% of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli prisons infected with scabies. Herzog taps Eisenkot to form new Israeli government. Yemen: At least 44 killed in Saudi strikes on Yemeni village. Aramco headquarters damaged in Riyadh. U.S.: Trump diagnoses midterms loss, talks future immigration deal with Democrats on 60 Minutes. And yet: Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Clean energy bill moves toward passage. Trump orders DOJ investigation of Democratic lawmakers. In Alaska Senate race, Peltola leads by "a couple of hundred votes." House Republican leaders expect impeachment of War Secretary Pete Hegseth. Chuck Schumer says he has enough Democratic support to become majority leader; Chris Van Hollen opens door to a challenge. ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at scheduled immigration appointment. U.S. deportation flight of Iranians abruptly canceled. Trump admin officials reportedly aware of Nvidia CEO's affair with Chinese spy. International: Attack on gas field causes widespread power outages in Iraq's Kurdish region. Sudanese Armed Forces advance against Rapid Support Forces in West Kordofan. SAF detains Bashir-era official wanted by International Criminal Court. Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34. Bangladeshi ex-PM Sheikh Hasina, who fled country in disgrace after repressing protesters, requests new passport to return. Drone attack on Colombian military base kills three soldiers. Guatemalan lawmaker, three police officers killed in attack. Mexico arrests alleged Jalisco cartel leader linked to 19 killings. Russian strikes cause power outages for hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians. Poland opens terrorism investigation after gunman kills six in Krakow. 200,000+ people march in Amsterdam demanding action against Israel. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. forces again target Qeshm Island: U.S. forces fired "projectiles" towards Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday night, causing at least four explosions, Iranian state media said. Iranian officials said U.S. forces targeted several areas outside residential and commercial zones on Qeshm. "No damage was caused to the island's vital and service infrastructure," Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Hormozgan province, told state broadcaster IRIB. Residents on Qeshm Island reported hearing several explosions late Sunday evening, Iranian state media reported. U.S. strikes affecting availability of essential medicines: Recent U.S. strikes have damaged 15 drug-manufacturing companies and eight distribution firms, Iran's Food and Drug Administration said. As a result of the attacks, Iran is facing difficulties in providing 37 out of some 700 types of essential medicine, an agency's spokesperson told the Tasnim news agency. Mojtaba Khamenei urges resolution on stalemate: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued new directives on ending the state of "neither war nor peace" with the U.S., Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said. "The supreme leader ordered us to end the no-war, no-peace situation," he said on Monday, according to Iranian media reports. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged Washington to accept Tehran's two-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and said there have been no changes in Iran's position. "American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own. Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results. Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell," Araghchi on X. Trump says renewed attack on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks progress: President Donald Trump told CNN in a phone interview that as long as Washington sees progress in negotiations with Tehran it is "highly unlikely it's going to be necessary" to resume strikes. Trump nevertheless added that the U.S. had identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, that it would strike if military action resumes. The prime minister of Qatar, which has helped lead mediation efforts to end the war, arrived in Washington, DC, on Monday to meet Trump and Vice President JD Vance. Iran hangs three men in connection with anti-government protests: In Karaj on Sunday, Iran hanged three men convicted on charges related to nationwide anti-government protests in January, state TV reported. The three were convicted of armed riot, damage to public properties, and cooperation with Israel and the United States during the demonstrations. Iran has hanged more than two dozen people on similar charges this year alone. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed three Palestinians--two in new attacks and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and injured 15 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,643 killed and 175,962 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,613 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,833, while 849 bodies have been recovered. Five Palestinians killed amid heavy rains: On Sunday, at least five Palestinians, including four children, were killed in Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, after a sand cliff collapsed onto makeshift tents where displaced families were sheltering, Al Jazeera reported. The sand cliff collapse was triggered by heavy winter rains. An unknown number of people are reportedly still missing under the massive pile of sand and rock. Civil defense workers and nearby residents searched through the rubble, largely working with their bare hands. "This is a scene that should shame the conscience of humanity," the Gaza Government Media Office said in a statement on Monday. 70,000 tents flood as winter storm hits Gaza: Around 70,000 tents were flooded within 12 hours when the first winter storm of the season hit Gaza this weekend, according to Gaza's Government Media Office. Civil Defense received over 2,100 distress calls and declared a maximum state of emergency. Dozens of displacement encampments--tents, shelters, and entire residential areas--were flooded by the heavy rains, Civil Defense said. In some areas, water levels rose 1.5 meters. In a , Save the Children said, "This is not simply the result of bad weather. Tents, shelter kits and fuel are waiting at Gaza's borders while children sleep in floodwater, because the Israeli authorities are blocking their entry. This is a choice, and children are paying the price. More than a year into the so-called ceasefire, it has failed to protect Palestinian children." Transport companies announce suspension of services: The Ministry of Health in Gaza said on Sunday it has received reports from a number of approved transport companies announcing the complete suspension of services. The companies attributed the decision to the accumulation of non-payment of their dues, and a large number of vehicles being put out of service due to frequent breakdowns, and an acute shortage of spare parts, oils, and tires. The Health Ministry warned of "serious and unprecedented repercussions that threaten the work of hospitals and primary health care centers." 80% of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli prisons infected with scabies: About 80% of Palestinians detained in Israeli prisons, including women and children, are infected with scabies, the Palestinian Prisoner's Society (PPS) on Sunday. Israeli authorities routinely deny adequate treatment, clothing, and hygiene facilities to Palestinian prisoners. Based on lawyers' visits throughout October and early November, PPS also documented violent raids every two to three days in some prison sections, with prisoners subjected to severe beatings, attacks by police dogs, rubber-coated bullets and gas. They also found systematic food deprivation, with prisoners receiving severely inadequate quantities and quality of food, and severe overcrowding, with prisoner forced to sleep on floors while guards confiscate mattresses during the day. Herzog taps Eisenkot to form new Israeli government: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday formally gave Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a new government. Eisenkot now has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension from the president. If he is unable to form a government, Netanyahu could then be given a chance to put together a coalition. If Netanyahu is also unable to do so, new elections could be called. Eisenkot has said that parties can join his coalition if they agree to four conditions: recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; a duty of national service for all; recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organization; and a commitment to destroying Hamas's military and governing capacity. Netanyahu's Likud Party won the most seats of any single party, while his wider coalition won 53 seats, short of a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat parliament. Eisenkot's Yashar party emerged as the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, won a total of 48 seats. Two parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel won an unprecedented 19 seats. Israel's new members of Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday evening. Netanyahu and his cabinet will remain in office in a caretaker capacity, with limited powers, until a new ruling coalition is formed. Yemen At least 44 killed in Saudi strikes on Yemeni village: Airstrikes blamed on Saudi Arabia that hit homes in a Yemeni village near the capital of Sana'a killed at least 44 people, including 21 children, the Health Ministry in Sana'a said on Sunday. It was one of the deadliest attacks in the latest phase of the war, to the Associated Press. The strikes on the village of al-Shariya, east of the capital, also wounded 40 people, including eight children and nine women, the Health Ministry said. Rescue teams are still searching for missing people, and the death toll could rise. At least 91 airstrikes targeted six Yemeni governorates in the 24 hours from Saturday to Sunday, Ansarallah military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a on Sunday. He added that the total number of Saudi-led coalition attacks since the latest escalation in the war in September was at 4,460. Aramco headquarters damaged in Riyadh: Several floors of Saudi oil giant Aramco's corporate office in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, were damaged on Sunday in what the energy ministry said was debris from an attempt to attack the building, to Reuters. Ansrallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree on Sunday that Ansarallah had hit Riyadh's financial district, where Aramco's headquarters is located, and other targets in response to recent Saudi attacks that have killed and injured dozens of people. U.S. News Trump diagnoses midterms loss, talks future immigration deal with Democrats on 60 Minutes: In an interview with 60 Minutes' Ross Douthat on Sunday, President Trump his party's historic midterm loss earlier in the week. In part, he attributed the loss to the Iran War, saying that voters "didn't like the war." "They didn't like the fact that gasoline went up," he said, while noting what he called the "great dislike...for Israel." In reference to a post-mortem from Vice President JD Vance posted on X last week, which singled out the Iran war, Trump said he would have made the same decision again, though he said he would have made the same post in Vance's position, and that he "liked" Vance's comments. Trump that his immigration-enforcement policy was "too tough" and likely cost his party in the midterms. He said he was open to a comprehensive immigration-reform deal that would secure the border, while allowing some immigrant workers to remain in the U.S. if they do not have a criminal record and have been living in the country for some time. And yet: Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff: On Friday, Trump Miller , previously his homeland security adviser and deputy chief of staff, will replace Susie Wiles as the White House chief of staff. In a Truth Social post, Trump said that Miller "gets it very good politically" and is a "great manager." Wiles likely wouldn't have been ousted if Republicans had performed better in the midterm elections, one source told Politico. And another source said that Trump was frustrated that she has acted as a "restraining bull." Miller, 41, has been a key adviser to Trump over both of his presidential terms and is the principal architect of Trump's hardline immigration policy. Clean energy bill moves toward passage: The Senate has released a so-called manager's amendment of a permitting-reform bill called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). The new version of the bill primarily seeks to address concerns around tribal rights. The clean-energy industry solidly supports BAAJA, though some environmental groups whose focus is blocking energy projects continue to object to it. The bill has the backing of Environment and Public Works Chair Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) and Ranking Member Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), as well as Energy and Natural Resources Chair Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah) and Ranking Member Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.). Backers of the bill are optimistic that it could pass within the next two weeks, and they worry that pushing it to the next session would doom it. The argument against the environmentalist objections is straightforward: Efforts to transition away from fossil fuels and toward clean energy by relying on litigation and regulation will backfire politically if those efforts drive up the costs of energy, as the midterms just demonstrated. Only by allowing clean energy to outbuild dirty energy can the transition be made feasible. That requires beating back some of the powerful community groups that have been able to block clean energy projects. The advocates further argue that the current laws obviously do not prevent the fossil-fuel industry from building dirty-energy infrastructure. Trump orders DOJ investigation of Democratic lawmakers: On Saturday, President Trump said that he ordered the Justice Department to look into "criminal acts" by Democratic lawmakers. In a Truth Social post, he said that Democrats' threats of investigations and impeachment are "extortion at the highest level." He singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), accusing her of threatening young conservatives. and said that "imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS." During an appearance on CNN's "State of the Union" on Sunday, Attorney General Todd Blanche Congress' oversight authority, but said that Democrats' rhetoric crossed a line. He refused to rule out the possibility that the DOJ would prosecute Democratic lawmakers for trying to investigate the Trump administration. Blanche said, "I would be very worried if I was a member" of the Oversight Committee. He added that the DOJ will provide legal defense to Trump officials facing scrutiny from Democrats. In Alaska Senate race, Peltola leads by "a couple of hundred votes": Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy a local radio station on Sunday that the state's Senate race remains "very close," with Democrat Mary Peltola up by roughly "a couple of hundred votes." Seventy percent of the votes are counted in the first round, after which ranked-choice voting preferences kick in. Further votes will be counted over the next two weeks. According to Decision Desk HQ, Peltola is barely leading Sen. Dan Sullivan. She has won about 48.2% of votes, and Sen. Sullivan has won 47.9%. Separately on Friday, Mary Peltola's campaign that it is suing the state to obtain access to records for absentee ballots that were rejected by Alaska's Division of Elections. The campaign claims that it sought access to the ballots multiple times but was denied, and that access is necessary to "ensure voters' lawful votes were properly counted." The state responded to the lawsuit in a press release on Friday, saying it was not constitutionally obligated to provide the information "in the manner requested by the campaign." House Republican leaders expect impeachment of War Secretary Pete Hegseth: House GOP leadership Republican defections to enable the impeachment of War Secretary Pete Hegseth , Axios reported. Outgoing Republicans have little to lose, and there is considerable animosity for Hegseth. Rep. Don Bacon , a retiring Republican from Nebraska, told Fox News that Hegseth didn't "have a lot of love" on the Hill. Rep. Thomas Massie plans to force an impeachment vote this week, accusing Hegseth of defying Congress, and of illegally continuing the Iran war. Hegseth has called the planned impeachment effort a "sham." Hegseth's removal by impeachment would require 67 votes in favor in the Senate. Chuck Schumer says he has enough Democratic support to become majority leader; Chris Van Hollen opens door to a challenge: Aides to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) the New York Times on Saturday that the 75-year-old has secured commitments from enough senators to win another term as leader of the Democratic Party's Senate Caucus. Schumer has served in that capacity since 2017, and previously served as Majority Leader from 2021 to 2025. The announcement follows a push to change the party's Senate leadership, with a movement underway to draft Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen, Politico Playbook reported on Monday. Von Hollen had previously declined to challenge Schumer, hinting at a presidential run instead, that he had "received an outpouring of calls and is now in active listening mode. The door is not shut." About a third of Democratic voters view Schumer favorably, according to a May poll from New York Times/Siena. ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at scheduled immigration appointment: ICE an 8-year-old boy as he was arriving at a scheduled immigration appointment in San Diego, Calif., last week, KPBS reported. A volunteer court observer filmed the incident, and said that she had "never watched a child by himself get detained in that manner." The boy, originally from Haiti, has lived in San Diego with his uncle since his father was deported in March 2025. The Department of Homeland Security says that his uncle lacked legal custody, so the boy was treated as an unaccompanied minor and taken into the custody of the Office of Refugee Resettlement "out of an abundance of caution." The San Diego Unified School district and other local officials demanded the boy's release to his uncle in a letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. U.S. deportation flight of Iranians abruptly canceled: At least eight Iranians were loaded onto a plane in Mesa, Ariz., in a deportation flight bound for Pakistan, before the flight was abruptly canceled, Ali Rahnama , a lawyer for the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund, . The administration said as recently as mid-October that it planned to deport Iranians to Iran through a third country, according to unsealed court documents. Trump admin officials reportedly aware of Nvidia CEO 's affair with Chinese spy: Secretary of State Marco Rubio the drafting of a classified memo warning administration officials that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese spy, the New York Times reported. The memo, circulated this spring ahead of Trump's trip to China in May, drew on electronic surveillance of Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang), a Chinese citizen and senior executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which bought about $2 billion in Nvidia chips and is suspected of helping smuggle restricted chips into China. U.S. officials concluded that Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. On Sunday, Nvidia opened an investigation in Huang after he acknowledged he had been intimate with her, with the company saying that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." Trump was briefed on the matter about a year ago and took no action. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Attack on gas field causes widespread power outages in Iraq 's Kurdish region: An attack on the Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq's Kurdish region was targeted by a drone attack late on Sunday, taking the facility offline and causing widespread power outages, the AP reported. No casualties were announced, and the extent of the damage was not immediately clear. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Sudanese Armed Forces advances against Rapid Support Forces in West Kordofan: On Sunday, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and its allies heavy battles with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Abu Minaiqir, about 34 miles north of El-Khuwei in West Kordofan, the Sudan Tribune reported. The SAF also said that it shot down a long-range drone near Wad Banda, its third interception in Kordofan in 72 hours, as it pushes west to secure routes for future operations in Darfur. SAF detains Bashir-era official wanted by International Criminal Court: The SAF on Sunday that it had detained Ahmed Haroun, chair of former President Omar al-Bashir's National Congress Party, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes and genocide in Darfur in the early 2000s, Reuters reported. It was unclear why the SAF moved against Haroun, whose Islamist movement has fought alongside it against the RSF. Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34: On Saturday, at least 34 people died when a wooden pirogue carrying migrants and refugees off the Loumpoul dunes in Senegal's Kebemer department, between Dakar and Saint-Louis. The Interior Ministry said that one person was rescued. Bangladeshi ex-PM Sheikh Hasina, who fled country in disgrace after repressing protesters, requests new passport to return: On Monday, former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina Bangladesh's embassy in New Delhi to issue her a new passport and national identity card, Reuters reported. It is the clearest indication yet that she plans to return to Bangladesh, where she would almost certainly surrender before a court. As prime minister, she ordered a deadly crackdown on 2024 student-led protests, and last year a Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in absentia for her role in the repression. During the protests, Hasina resigned as prime minister and fled to India. Drone attack on Colombian military base kills three soldiers: A drone strike on a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, in northern Colombia, three soldiers and wounded at least 16 other soldiers, the Colombian armed forces said on Saturday. Colombian officials the National Liberation Army for the attack. The drone strike follows a strike on the group inside Venezuelan territory last month. It is the latest in a wave of attacks on security forces since conservative President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August. Since assuming power, de la Espriella has canceled peace talks and escalated military operations against armed groups. Guatemalan lawmaker, three police officers killed in attack: Gunmen Guatemalan congressman Julio Cesar Portillo Paz, of the right-wing National Unity of Hope Party, and three National Civil Police officers in an attack in Rio Hondo, Zacapa, on Friday, Reuters reported. President Bernardo Arevalo ordered security forces to assist prosecutors in identifying those responsible. The killings come three weeks after former anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa was shot dead in Guatemala City, fueling fears of a new wave of political assassinations. Mexico arrests alleged Jalisco cartel leader linked to 19 killings: Mexican forces Rafael Álvarez, the alleged head of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel's "Los Rs" cell, along with 19 others in an operation in Zapopan on Sunday. The operation relied on intelligence from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, the Mexican Navy said. Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said that Álvarez, who was wounded in a shootout during the arrest and faces a U.S. extradition warrant, is linked to at least 19 killings, including last year's murder of Carlos Manzo, the mayor of Uruapan, in Michoacan. Russian strikes cause power outages for hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians: Russian strikes on energy facilities have caused power outages for more than 600,000 people in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region and 250,000 in the Kharkiv, Ukrainian officials and energy company DTEK . The strikes followed a huge Russian assault on Saturday that cut power in five regions, which President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said was aimed at pressuring Kyiv ahead of U.S.-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi this week. Poland opens terrorism investigation after gunman kills six in Krakow: The National Prosecutor's Office announced that it is investigating the deadly Krakow shooting as a terrorist attack. On Saturday, a 24-year-old Polish gunman opened fire in Krakow's historic city center, killing six people, including a British national, and wounding 15 others. After the attack, police found the bodies of the suspect's parents and sister at his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski. He was wounded in a gunfight with police, and died of his wounds on Monday. 200,000+ people march in Amsterdam demanding action against Israel: On Sunday, more than 200,000 people marched through Amsterdam in a protest on the Dutch government to halt all arms sales to Israel and to tighten trade restrictions with the country over its genocidal war on Gaza. It would weaken Tribes’ and the general public’s ability to challenge polluting projects in court ― allowing unaccountable, greedy corporations to speed up data center and fracked natural gas pipeline construction. **Let’s be clear: This bill is a gift to Big Oil and Big Tech.** It makes it easier to build fossil fuel infrastructure while undermining clean water and national environmental policy acts. It would also strip away Tribes’ and the general public’s right to give input and sue to stop polluting projects and to protect culturally significant areas.
As one of the last acts of this Republican-controlled Congress, we cannot allow our government to lock in fossil fuel and Big Tech dominance for generations to come.
[**Add your name now to demand Congress reject this handout to greedy, polluting corporations.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39Vp4gkIh90ovDrixVFaBLc32CpAaZ5zvifbp2V-udQrW5saMRU-IM2UZ7k_GWdTmiORkMeRnWP1bP5HYDRUtEQqbZwLduuvdp6i95rMwFGhoYmP8pqGtdoIaNiL3o6LJvAWq5G-DtBeP5NTmWTUgJQQwJJAObqSuB0BomuKuPDJFmRbaEeYjTryyf3wVbgefWvCIDiSQS_d4u67oe93NY2Uwz8g2aZ7_wnriaQ3TgdqQyPgUKJHYegkh4MPp16xdIDWML9lHvaoB9bg5JNwTruaPuZyot-ZqxiHHvOmfUgPRugB0Agt92lbE1DF8h7hEZORYZhUbxJjZo4vTxuXN9T63AlO_r9soekI6CmoZArVLckxwMFamr7wpVv9I8x-kRorev-34V5a_iqf7JZH5E7o5ic8uQ_8Dvdca5NXXnXe3KZzQzXcYhBZLPYl_JEyos/4vl/OmtdkXjnRve61XE_ccYm6Q/h3/h001.RnWqLQ9s7QWVQWoqG3mc0Fh8NiHxjiDyF_WotnZy4l4)
**Growing up in Detroit by the Marathon Oil Refinery and other corporate polluters, I know what it’s like to live in a frontline community treated as a sacrifice zone.**
Tribal and environmental review processes were put in place to protect our air, land, water, and communities from this type of corporate overreach. Don’t let Congress wipe them away less than a week after an election where the American people demanded fundamental change.
With you in the fight for better,
Rashida

name: Elizabeth Dempsey Beggs
subject: WE DID IT!
body:
Thanks to you!

| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| |
# We did it!
---
| |
Friends,Our goal was always to flip Virginia’s First District blue—and we did.
To everyone who donated, volunteered, knocked doors, made calls, shared our message, or encouraged me along the way: thank you. You gave your time, your resources, and your heart to this campaign, and that work mattered.
Every conversation you had, every dollar you donated, and every door you knocked moved the needle. You helped register voters, bring more people into the process, and build the momentum that made this victory possible. Our campaign was part of a larger effort here in Virginia and a wave of people across the country deciding that a better future was worth showing up for.
People are standing up and saying no to corruption, no to injustice, and no to the undue influence of money in politics. They are demanding a government that answers to the people it serves. You helped carry that message forward.
Here in Virginia, we are one of three states with off-year state elections mean another opportunity to turn that energy into action, and protect the work we have done going into 2028. There is so much we can do right here at home to support working families, protect our rights, and fight for a future that is fair for everyone. I’m looking forward to continuing that work alongside you.
But today, take a moment to celebrate. Pat yourself on the back. Be proud of what you helped accomplish. Organizing takes patience, persistence, and faith that your effort matters—even when you can’t immediately see the results.
This week, we got to see them.I believe history will remember the people who refused to give up and kept showing up for their neighbors. I am grateful to have stood alongside you.
With gratitude,
Elizabeth Dempsey Beggs

clean_body: Thanks to you! | | | | | | | | | | | | | We did it! | | Friends,Our goal was always to flip Virginia’s First District blue—and we did. To everyone who donated, volunteered, knocked doors, made calls, shared our message, or encouraged me along the way: thank you. You gave your time, your resources, and your heart to this campaign, and that work mattered. Every conversation you had, every dollar you donated, and every door you knocked moved the needle. You helped register voters, bring more people into the process, and build the momentum that made this victory possible. Our campaign was part of a larger effort here in Virginia and a wave of people across the country deciding that a better future was worth showing up for. People are standing up and saying no to corruption, no to injustice, and no to the undue influence of money in politics. They are demanding a government that answers to the people it serves. You helped carry that message forward. Here in Virginia, we are one of three states with off-year state elections mean another opportunity to turn that energy into action, and protect the work we have done going into 2028. There is so much we can do right here at home to support working families, protect our rights, and fight for a future that is fair for everyone. I’m looking forward to continuing that work alongside you. But today, take a moment to celebrate. Pat yourself on the back. Be proud of what you helped accomplish. Organizing takes patience, persistence, and faith that your effort matters—even when you can’t immediately see the results. This week, we got to see them.I believe history will remember the people who refused to give up and kept showing up for their neighbors. I am grateful to have stood alongside you. With gratitude, Elizabeth Dempsey Beggs | | | | | | | | | | | This email was sent to mailto:dpwillis67@gmail.com Elizabeth For Virgina 11089 Summer Breeze Dr Ashland VA 23005 Ashland, VA 23005 USA

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Not even 2 days after the Democratic Party flipped both the U.S. House and
Senate in a monumental blue wave, Democrats on the House Judiciary
Committee were already back to making weak proposals on social media:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261109.yxFFZv&refcode=em20261109-38421&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38421%2E1203867%2EfofGzm ]Tweet by House Judiciary Dems: It’s time for ICE to take the masks off,
turn the body cameras on, and start answering to the American people who
pay for their bloated budget.

The post got a ton of negative feedback, and for good reason. Most
comments communicated the same thing: abolishing ICE is the bare minimum
we expect from Democrats now that they’ve won power back.

Voters are tired of Democrats acting like Diet Republicans, as if it’s
okay for ICE to terrorize and hurt our loved ones as long as they’re
unmasked and wearing body cameras.

ICE is a rogue paramilitary force that has time and again violated the
rights of citizens and non-citizens alike. People made it loud and clear
in the midterms that they reject Trump’s gestapo and their cruelty: it’s
time to abolish this department and hold it accountable for the death and
trauma it’s inflicted on our communities.

We need to make it crystal clear to the Democratic Party: no more
watered-down half measures. No more mealy-mouthed statements and
‘strongly-worded’ letters. It’s time to fight back, seek justice, and
deliver results.

Thankfully, we have 8 new Justice Democrats heading to Congress in January
who are already speaking out about this and recommitting to abolish ICE.
