First, the ultimate battle isn’t about politics or parties. It’s about truth, and the freedom to speak it. ADF exists to remove the obstacles between people and the Gospel. We protect the first freedoms that keep the door open so that all might be free. With God’s grace, we do that regardless of which party is in power. Second, we play the long game. The terrain changes, but the strategy does not. We anticipated this shift, though we hoped it wouldn’t be this big, and that is why—with your partnership—we have pressed so hard in the courts these past few years. We will likely see more hostility toward truth in the days ahead. But we also expect new opportunities to set precedents, especially in states with leaders hostile to human flourishing. Losses at the ballot box in Nevada and Virginia, where voters enshrined a right to abortion in their state constitutions, signal what kinds of policies might soon be attempted elsewhere. We will continue to contend for the sanctity of every woman’s life and that of her unborn child. But truth won on Tuesday, too. It can never be erased, only rediscovered or rejected. And in several states, voters rediscovered the truth that men and women are different. Biology isn’t red or blue. Building on our major victory at the U.S. Supreme Court this year, voters in Arizona and Nebraska approved measures to protect girls’ sports. Arizona’s extended those protections to women’s private spaces. Nebraska’s wrote its women’s sports law into the state constitution. You might expect that from Nebraska or even Arizona. Then came Colorado and Washington. In Colorado, two measures are leading: one protecting girls’ sports, the other protecting children from dangerous transition surgeries. In my home state of Washington, voters appear to have approved a measure protecting girls’ sports. Voters are responding to the stories of girls who paid the price. In Puyallup, Washington, then-15-year-old wrestler Kallie Keeler was sexually assaulted by a male competitor whom state and school policy allowed to compete against her. The state told her it could happen again. Her emergency petition is pending before the U.S. Supreme Court. And in Camas, Washington, a male athlete who switched to the girls’ cross-country team midyear took the final qualifying spot from a deserving young woman from Puyallup High School. He will compete in the women’s state finals this Saturday. I don’t want you to miss this, friend. In 2014, when ADF took on the lie of gender ideology to uphold biological reality, few were with us. Public opinion was at best mixed. This week, the American people crossed political and ideological lines to say otherwise. This tells us the American people aren’t ready to abandon truth. Getting here took hard work, alliance-building, and persuasion. Tragically, it also took many young women paying the cost of a lie. If working at ADF has shown me anything, it is that sometimes you have to lose before you can win. But truth always defeats darkness, and lies have a way of producing harms that become impossible to deny. We are not afraid. We walk into the wind, because that is where God has called us. This is not a time for despair. Hebrews 6:18-19 reminds us it is impossible for God to lie, and it calls the hope we have in Him “a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.” That hope is why the Lord has called ADF to keep the door open for the Gospel. You and I contend for His truth so that all might be free to find that hope and spend eternity with Him. The terrain has changed. The calling has not. Let’s go. | | [DOUBLE MY GIFT](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckb2OnTAQRp_GdFz5D8wtKCIRlGYT5U8prcEewFmDLXvYvH50k00eYNujoxkdfT-e7BOEGM7tIxw4FlptqZZ2rATPWH9elbZEe9h2LFZy2bdCtPxuwVF4Qauh8aN3HoRrcBTmrqVW_aCafexFxwe1dgusRvNuWZcV-94YPsil5x6aMD7uCcHvwnAhxU2CFsa7brkrvshVM80hYqFbwXwtMTg4CerzmorDm0tHE8edKFem3jE5MzmDXyNuEG-pbEzO9co5FWJy9ukEwvYAcvtDVXNNV3HokkemJiG4FoPhtgwdZ7K_6LB_BaamE17JgT5cB1MTHhDiK3RwZAjbydSUU6UWIzoK6WwhZ4T_VjoJT2Jq-vDp-9f39rNpv3yb23_9TRl9_hViDLU3TPPt8eBPIb1lkZdR_g4AAP__rjWaog)

Their wonderful love is the reason I do this job and it is for their future and the future of all the kids in Eastern Washington that we work so hard.
I’m a proud Eastern Washington kid and it is an honor to represent its outstanding people in Congress. There is no better place in the world to live, work, and raise a family than the Inland Northwest. I will continue to do everything I can to keep it that way. I worry about what the election results will mean for the future of the country, but I know - I absolutely, positively know - that the best days for America lie ahead. We will make sure of it.
Now, it’s time to get back to work. I’m excited. We have a state and a country to fight for, and a future to build.
My heartfelt thanks again for your trust and support. In a year like this more than ever - we would not have won without YOU.

Washington is buzzing — the left celebrating, Republicans still shell-shocked, everyone asking what comes next. But the church has a different answer: worship. We put on the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness. And there is heaviness — no question. Demonic forces have ascended. The darkness is real and we’re not pretending otherwise. But there is still One on the throne. One to whom _every_ knee will bow — every principality, every power, every name that gets sworn in this January. This Friday, He is who we are praising.

#### _**[Tuesday's election was a historic victory, but I'm not interested in spending the next two years celebrating while Trump and his cronies keep screwing over the American people. That's why I built Endless Urgency. We're creating an independent media platform that confronts right-wing lies, exposes corruption, and helps build a Democratic Party that actually delivers for working people. If you believe in this mission, become a paid subscriber for just $8/month and help us keep going](https://substack.com/redirect/b791cb57-43a9-4108-a582-e2cde1facba0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):**_

_Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know._
* * *
It's been almost a week since the midterm election, and you'd think that after a historic drubbing, the likes of which we haven't seen in 50 years, the Republican Party and its MAGA media machine might have learned something.
Yet, it seems they learned absolutely nothing, and I can't help but chuckle at the arrogance and stupidity of those incompetent boobs who stumbled their way into running this country. If you can even call what they're doing, "running."
I watched Trump on 60 Minutes last night, and he doubled down on the great standing of America, as if nothing happened on Tuesday. Then he took a few swipes at his own Vice President, for good measure.
Sure, I think J.D. Vance is an incompetent boob too, but to his credit, he's been trying to put some distance between himself and the war in Iran. So what does Donald Trump do? He goes on national television and says Vance was a key to its planning, welding him to the single most unpopular thing Trump's done in this disastrous second term. What a betrayal. In Trump World, loyalty only ever flows in one direction.
He's talking up Pete Hegseth like the guy is Eisenhower and might keep that moron at the Pentagon. He also elevated Stephen Miller to chief of staff, which tells you exactly where the attacks on immigrant communities are headed.
But nothing captures this moment better than Todd Blanche.
Donald Trump's personal defense attorney, now the Attorney General of the United States. Days after voters delivered a historic rebuke, Trump went on television and announced that Blanche was now the personal attorney for Stephen Miller, and for anybody else Democrats try to investigate for corruption and abuse of power.
The top law enforcement officer in the country whose job is to serve you, the American people - overseeing national security, civil law, and the agencies meant to protect our country - is openly declaring that his job is to protect the president's inner circle from accountability. Talk about a cabal of disgusting people circling the wagons.
And this corruption burns straight through the MAGA media machine, too. I've been on Newsmax and everywhere else debating these guys every day since the election. And everywhere I go, it's the same crap: _Democrats are communists. Abdul El-Sayed is a jihadist. They 're going to take your job and give it to an immigrant. They're going to steal your kids in the middle of the night and turn them trans._
It's deeply embarrassing, and all they can do is default to their programming - racist, homophobic, transphobic, anti-woman slop - because they don't have a single real answer for anything. I'm going to keep walking into those studios and calling it out to their faces, and the paid subscribers to this newsletter are a big part of why I can.
* * *
#### _**[Here's why your support matters: Every time I walk into a right-wing studio and challenge their bullshit, every time we expose corruption or push Democrats to fight harder, we're doing the work Endless Urgency was built to do. We're not here to repeat party talking points or make excuses for politicians. We're here to tell the truth, hold powerful people accountable, and make sure this moment becomes something bigger than one election. Our work stays free because people like you choose to support it. For $8/month, you can help us grow our team, expand our reach, and keep showing up where these conversations need to happen most.](https://substack.com/redirect/b791cb57-43a9-4108-a582-e2cde1facba0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/b791cb57-43a9-4108-a582-e2cde1facba0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
The closest anyone on the right has come to reality is Ron DeSantis saying the GOP needs new ideas. He doesn't have any either, but he's the only one smart enough to notice.
Meanwhile, Trump isn't going to work with Democrats on anything meaningful. Anything we pass that helps the American people, he'll veto, or he'll sign it because he's been shamed into it, just like the Epstein Files bill last year.
Say what you will about the Democratic Party, but when we lost to Trump in 2024, we looked inward. Sure, we had our idiotic infighting and messes like the Graham Platner fiasco, but we pulled it together when it mattered most, as the last group of people in American politics who give a damn about decency, democracy, and an economy that works for you instead of the billionaire class.
I was naive enough to think a beating like this might make Republicans look in the mirror for half a second. Maybe Trump won't be satisfied until Democrats are winning Arkansas and Idaho.
So here's my message to Democrats: We have the wind at our backs and a wounded opponent who doesn't understand why they won in 2024, doesn't understand why they lost in 2026, and has no idea what to do next, in front of us.
A rabid dog is running the White House, and the corruption, the racist memes, and the construction on the ballroom will all continue. Nothing changes unless we shape it.
With the House and the Senate, we finally have the power to do that. We can halt this agenda, end this war, and take back Congress's authority over tariffs. We can pass basic shit that improves people's lives, like raising the minimum wage, and bringing back the healthcare subsidies so premiums stop doubling and tripling.
If Trump vetoes it, make him own the veto, and make Republicans own it every time they hide behind the filibuster.
We also need to put the new voices front and center. I'd better see James Talarico on TV every chance he gets, like I did when he was on SNL this weekend. And I'd better see all of these new faces out there selling this agenda, taking back control of the narrative, and getting through to voters. This is our chance to expose how corrupt Trump and the Republicans are and to prove that our government can be a force for good.
Something generational is happening. Because we elected so many Democrats in their 30s and 40s, the average age in the Senate is dropping from about 68 and a half to 62. It's still too old, but such a monumental drop in one election must mean something.
We should go for broke, recruiting candidates everywhere, recruiting younger ones. Trump will be gone in two years, one way or another, and both parties have a jump ball for their future.
But we can never forget that the average American is hurting right now, and we shouldn't be cocky about this win. The only reason we won is because Trump broke every promise to make your life better. He made his own life better and his own net worth bigger, but not yours. The real work begins now. Democrats must earn back the trust and faith of the American people. We must convince them that the government can work for you. And we will do that by delivering on the promises we made and restoring the purpose of what we do, which is to be of service to all.
If you think the pendulum can't swing right back, you are dead wrong. If we fuck this moment up, if we take for granted this opportunity that the people have entrusted us with, it'll swing back hard, and people will turn to someone even more craven than Trump.
#### _**[The pendulum swings back when people stop paying attention, and I'm not going to stop. I'll be in those studios every day holding these people's feet to the fire, and paid subscribers are how I keep doing it. If this moment matters to you, join them.](https://substack.com/redirect/b791cb57-43a9-4108-a582-e2cde1facba0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
Love you guys.
With urgency,
--Mike

In Trump World, loyalty only ever flows in one direction. He's talking up Pete Hegseth like the guy is Eisenhower and might keep that moron at the Pentagon. He also elevated Stephen Miller to chief of staff, which tells you exactly where the attacks on immigrant communities are headed. But nothing captures this moment better than Todd Blanche. Donald Trump's personal defense attorney, now the Attorney General of the United States. Days after voters delivered a historic rebuke, Trump went on television and announced that Blanche was now the personal attorney for Stephen Miller, and for anybody else Democrats try to investigate for corruption and abuse of power. The top law enforcement officer in the country whose job is to serve you, the American people - overseeing national security, civil law, and the agencies meant to protect our country - is openly declaring that his job is to protect the president's inner circle from accountability. Talk about a cabal of disgusting people circling the wagons. And this corruption burns straight through the MAGA media machine, too. I've been on Newsmax and everywhere else debating these guys every day since the election. And everywhere I go, it's the same crap: Democrats are communists. Abdul El-Sayed is a jihadist. They 're going to take your job and give it to an immigrant. They're going to steal your kids in the middle of the night and turn them trans. It's deeply embarrassing, and all they can do is default to their programming - racist, homophobic, transphobic, anti-woman slop - because they don't have a single real answer for anything. I'm going to keep walking into those studios and calling it out to their faces, and the paid subscribers to this newsletter are a big part of why I can. The closest anyone on the right has come to reality is Ron DeSantis saying the GOP needs new ideas. He doesn't have any either, but he's the only one smart enough to notice. Meanwhile, Trump isn't going to work with Democrats on anything meaningful. Anything we pass that helps the American people, he'll veto, or he'll sign it because he's been shamed into it, just like the Epstein Files bill last year. Say what you will about the Democratic Party, but when we lost to Trump in 2024, we looked inward. Sure, we had our idiotic infighting and messes like the Graham Platner fiasco, but we pulled it together when it mattered most, as the last group of people in American politics who give a damn about decency, democracy, and an economy that works for you instead of the billionaire class. I was naive enough to think a beating like this might make Republicans look in the mirror for half a second. Maybe Trump won't be satisfied until Democrats are winning Arkansas and Idaho. So here's my message to Democrats: We have the wind at our backs and a wounded opponent who doesn't understand why they won in 2024, doesn't understand why they lost in 2026, and has no idea what to do next, in front of us. A rabid dog is running the White House, and the corruption, the racist memes, and the construction on the ballroom will all continue. Nothing changes unless we shape it. With the House and the Senate, we finally have the power to do that. We can halt this agenda, end this war, and take back Congress's authority over tariffs. We can pass basic shit that improves people's lives, like raising the minimum wage, and bringing back the healthcare subsidies so premiums stop doubling and tripling. If Trump vetoes it, make him own the veto, and make Republicans own it every time they hide behind the filibuster. We also need to put the new voices front and center. I'd better see James Talarico on TV every chance he gets, like I did when he was on SNL this weekend. And I'd better see all of these new faces out there selling this agenda, taking back control of the narrative, and getting through to voters. This is our chance to expose how corrupt Trump and the Republicans are and to prove that our government can be a force for good. Something generational is happening. Because we elected so many Democrats in their 30s and 40s, the average age in the Senate is dropping from about 68 and a half to 62. It's still too old, but such a monumental drop in one election must mean something. We should go for broke, recruiting candidates everywhere, recruiting younger ones. Trump will be gone in two years, one way or another, and both parties have a jump ball for their future. But we can never forget that the average American is hurting right now, and we shouldn't be cocky about this win. The only reason we won is because Trump broke every promise to make your life better. He made his own life better and his own net worth bigger, but not yours. The real work begins now. Democrats must earn back the trust and faith of the American people. We must convince them that the government can work for you. And we will do that by delivering on the promises we made and restoring the purpose of what we do, which is to be of service to all. If you think the pendulum can't swing right back, you are dead wrong. If we fuck this moment up, if we take for granted this opportunity that the people have entrusted us with, it'll swing back hard, and people will turn to someone even more craven than Trump. ** Love you guys. With urgency, --Mike Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. body:
Good news and bad news

---
| | | | Peter,
---
I’m writing to you this morning with good news and bad news. The bad news is that this race has not yet been called, and we remain behind Salazar by 1,116 votes.
**The good news is that this race is not over, and we are not conceding.** That margin is just 0.46 percentage points, putting us within range of an automatic recount under Florida law. While we have ground to gain, mail-in ballots and cure affidavits remain to be processed, and we remain staunchly committed to making sure every single vote is counted.
[**_We need your help to do just that. We must all rally together to make sure all voices can be heard, all votes can be counted, and our democracy can work as intended. Can you rush a split donation between Linda Sánchez and me, even $5, to our recount fund?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143177177/659335925/-498537557?refcode=BLU_EM_SAN_2026-11-09_01&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85ODI2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNjdjOGU2My02N2RjLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2ExYjg5NjIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eeu30jL0iYh-80UNKImnAb5omPWJMNRq2ds7e76JFk8=)

San Francisco made history. Here's why it matters right now. | |
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143178664/659341032/-568742666?amount=10&refcode=sw_fr_em_30DO_261109_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDY5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MWQ5NzM5Zi02OWRjLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2ExYjg5NjIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wiixxDcM1SG-YqFCqjQPNzHZ5gBl7XzTOPo02Uh3mW8=) Peter, when I moved to San Francisco nearly 30 years ago, I was looking for a place where I could live openly and authentically. I found so much more than that. _I found my home._ And now, San Francisco has elected an openly LGBTQ person to Congress for the first time in its history. **That matters. Especially right now, when Donald Trump and his allies are doing everything they can to roll back the LGBTQ rights we've fought for.** We have to stand up to them and we have to refuse to back down. clean_body: | | = We put up one hell of a fight, and it paid off. The people of Hampton Roads voted to send me back to Congress. This win belongs to every donor, volunteer, staffer, and voter who refused to give up on this district. You knocked doors in the rain, made calls after long workdays, and chipped in when it would have been easier to sit this one out. That’s what carried us across the finish line. We didn’t get here easily. MAGA poured more than $8 million into this race to keep VA-02 under Republican control. We were outspent and underestimated. We didn’t do it alone. Democrats needed to flip three seats to take back the House. We exceeded that by a mile, and VA-02 is part of the reason why. For the first time in two years, there will be a serious check on the most corrupt administration in American history. Thanks to your support, we now have the power to defend our Constitution and our core American values. There’s a lot of work ahead. We need to make healthcare affordable, lower costs for families, combat corruption at the highest levels, do right by our men and women in uniform, and protect Medicare and Social Security. I’ll keep fighting for the things that matter most right here at home, from the Chesapeake Bay to the military families who call Hampton Roads home. I’ll work every single day to earn the trust you’ve placed in me. You’ll hear from me again soon. With gratitude, Congresswoman-elect Elaine Luria P.S. | | The ARI Briefing * November 2026 | [](https://us.list-manage.com/nkdB2jRgUz2?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)

# AI Goes to the Ballot Box
Midterm results, frontier AI oversight, and chip security
[](https://us.list-manage.com/13E0eUdRY1s?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
The 2026 midterms made one thing clear: AI issues are front and center for voters. From Senate races to local ballot measures, AI and data centers emerged as a major issue this election, with 56% of voters telling the NBC News Exit Poll that AI and data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress ([TIME](https://us.list-manage.com/Hiy6BgElSJA?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)).
In the words of ARI President Brad Carson, "What we just witnessed was an AI earthquake. Voters just sent a clear message that they want rules for AI and data centers" ([Axios](https://us.list-manage.com/2g4V8NU9nJK?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)).
Today's newsletter highlights some of the polling takeaways, the victory night speeches, and the outcomes of this year's election as we look ahead to the next Congress. Here's the latest.
| | The Midterms | 01
---|---
## Voters Send a Message on AI
Exit polls and local ballot measures show concern about AI and data centers across party lines
[](https://us.list-manage.com/RlFWavmaRpB?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
On November 3, voters nationwide weighed in on AI at nearly every level of the ballot. According to the [NBC News Exit Poll](https://us.list-manage.com/qxqAmDWpQ7Y?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), 76% of voters oppose building data centers in their communities, and 57% say AI will do more harm than good.
The same concerns showed up on local ballots. Ten states put more than 40 data center questions before voters, [according to Ballotpedia](https://us.list-manage.com/aoXCLnV_P4Y?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), including 21 in Ohio. ARI President Brad Carson, who tracked the results throughout election night, found just one county that appears to have voted to allow more data center development ([WIRED](https://us.list-manage.com/19CzvYTU3jW?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)).
But concerns weren't limited to data centers. In an October [Reuters/Ipsos poll](https://us.list-manage.com/dT87vb9Sj6e?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), a bipartisan majority of voters, including 80% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans, said they support stricter government regulation of AI. A late-September [AP-NORC poll](https://us.list-manage.com/ynIokkTnZ2y?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) found that 64% of U.S. adults, including 76% of Democrats and 54% of Republicans, believe AI is developing too quickly.
"Voters in both parties delivered the same verdict tonight. This is a crushing blow to the AI industry's anti-regulatory efforts to buy a Congress that would look the other way."Brad Carson, ARI President, to [WIRED](https://us.list-manage.com/rJs3Ibd0YaG?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
[Read more in WIRED ->](https://us.list-manage.com/fmb_PDON0xm?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | Election Night | 02
---|---
## On Election Night, Candidates Highlight Winning Message on AI
From Texas to South Carolina to Virginia, winning candidates used their victory speeches to deliver a message on AI
[](https://us.list-manage.com/1AA6jGjES6E?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
It wasn't just voters who spoke out on Election Day about AI safety and data centers. As the night stretched on, results came in and races were called, winning candidates used their victory speeches to highlight their commitment to building AI guardrails for the American public.
Tuesday night's victory speeches followed a midterm election that featured a surge of ads on tech and AI issues. By one count, Democrats spent over [$100 million](https://us.list-manage.com/kIeqtrDmqzc?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) on broadcast ads casting their opponents as being overly cozy with Big Tech and data centers. Analysis from the [Tech Oversight Project](https://us.list-manage.com/jBD5wPRp6at?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) found that at least 130 federal and gubernatorial races aired anti-tech or anti-data center ads this cycle, a dramatic increase over previous election cycles.
In their victory speeches, candidates showed AI wasn't just a campaign slogan, but a commitment to governing tech responsibly and protecting the public from AI harms. For a rundown of how winning candidates talked about AI on election night, check out our [video compilation of victory speech mentions here](https://us.list-manage.com/N9F_ga43m_5?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf).
"Meanwhile, the titans of Silicon Valley dig bunkers for themselves and warn that the artificial intelligence they're creating risks human extinction. And amidst these challenges of unprecedented consequence and complexity, though we rightly celebrate tonight's historic victory, we've been too long mired in a small and selfish politics bought by big money, unmoored from fixed moral principles, and resigned to intractable division."Senator Jon Ossoff
---
[Watch the victory speeches ->](https://us.list-manage.com/xJdfZVfDClq?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | On the Hill | 03
---|---
## Civil Society Groups Urge Follow Through on Campaign Promises
Coalition letter of 50+ civil society groups urges appointment of AI guardrail champions to committees in 120th Congress
On Thursday, a coalition of more than 50 civil society organizations [sent a letter](https://us.list-manage.com/iW_Ek_LGZ0s?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), first reported by [The Washington Post](https://us.list-manage.com/qMVjgrNuqVk?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), to Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, urging them to appoint lawmakers committed to strong AI safeguards to key committee and subcommittee leadership positions in the 120th Congress.
After a midterm election in which AI emerged as a major campaign issue, the coalition urged Democratic leaders to prioritize lawmakers who support binding federal AI regulations and oppose efforts to override state AI protections. Americans for Responsible Innovation, Encode, the Tech Oversight Project, and Demand Progress co-led the coalition letter.
"As a coalition of civil society organizations that support AI safeguards, we were strongly encouraged by the campaign-trail attention to AI policy addressing voter concerns regarding AI risks to families, workers, and communities. As you plan to take leadership of the House and Senate, we write today to urge you to address those concerns by appointing lawmakers who make strong, forward-looking commitments to advancing robust AI guardrails to positions of leadership in the new Congress."Nov. 5 coalition letter
---
After a campaign season where candidates ran ads on AI, talked about safeguards on the campaign trail, and highlighted their AI stances on victory night, it's clear that the incoming class of lawmakers is primed to act on the issue and will be looking for leadership that prioritizes AI safeguards.
[Read the letter ->](https://us.list-manage.com/ulKpF6ZiJfb?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)

## Keeping Pace with the Frontier
An early warning system for AI that builds AI
By Aaron Dorshow and Iskandar Haykel
[](https://us.list-manage.com/CyeSlycyYzz?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
AI is playing an increasingly important role in building the next generation of AI. [Anthropic recently reported](https://us.list-manage.com/I4VVTDlm2Eg?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) that, as of August 2026, Claude led 26% of the company's AI research and development activities, up from around 1% in March. OpenAI [is aiming](https://us.list-manage.com/e9lpUPIB6QP?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to create an automated "AI researcher" by March 2028.
In [Keeping Pace with the Frontier](https://us.list-manage.com/J0Y5prchKlc?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), ARI policy analyst Aaron Dorshow and Associate Director of Policy Iskandar Haykel argue that if AI progress accelerates faster than safety science, shorter release windows will leave less time and opportunity for the testing and research needed to keep the public safe. Today, only frontier developers know how fast their internal models are progressing, and the public mostly learns about it when companies choose to share. Drawing on ARI's blueprint, they propose a federal early warning system to change that.
| Quarterly filingsMajor frontier AI developers would file confidential reports with a new government agency on how they use AI in four areas: data and training inputs, algorithmic and architectural design, experimentation and research direction, and safety and oversight operations.
---
Material shiftsBetween filings, developers would report major changes, such as fully automating a research loop, within four business days.
Public reportingThe agency would periodically publish aggregate reports on AI research automation across the industry, while individual filings remain confidential to protect security and intellectual property.

## Securing America's Most Advanced AI Chips
ARI urges the President to endorse the Chip Security Act
[](https://us.list-manage.com/mVfDsMvHp3Y?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
On October 26, ARI sent a letter, first reported by [The Hill](https://us.list-manage.com/RfQ_PKDfhTG?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), urging President Trump to endorse the Chip Security Act. The bill, introduced by Sen. Tom Cotton (R-AR) in May 2025, would require the Commerce Department to mandate a location-verification mechanism for AI chips subject to export controls. Chip exporters would be required to report to the Commerce Department if their products were diverted from their intended destination or tampered with.
"Your endorsement of the Chip Security Act would send a clear message to America's competitors like China, and adversaries like Russia and Iran looking to acquire some of America's most powerful technologies: the United States will defend its technological edge and go after any illicit access to the advanced chips that power it."Brad Carson, in ARI's letter to the President
---
The letter comes as the United States and China prepare for new AI talks, with the first AI-specific meeting scheduled for November. ARI also continues to support the AI safety notification system proposed by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, featured in last month's Briefing.
[Read more in The Hill ->](https://us.list-manage.com/hNVuOWu4mAu?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---

New policy leadership and new roles are open.
We're excited to [welcome Chris Borges](https://us.list-manage.com/_q3Ui4s4d1J?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to ARI as our new Director of Policy, where he'll focus on AI's impact on labor, education, and government modernization. Chris joins us from CSIS and Epic Systems. We also [welcomed Noah Rudolph](https://us.list-manage.com/ouxGCvLoYyQ?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) as ARI's Policy Chief of Staff. Noah comes to ARI after consulting for the Office of Strategic Capital and the National Security Innovation Network.
As the team grows, ARI is hiring for several roles. If someone in your network belongs on our team, please pass these along.

# [Jensen Huang's Chinese spy-affair bombshell hits Nvidia stock](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia shares fell 5-6% Monday after CEO Jensen Huang **[admitted an affair with MegaSpeed executive Alice Huang,](https://substack.com/redirect/c4ae5872-cf9f-493a-a972-e48f29ea7516?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** whom **[U.S. officials identify as a Chinese intelligence asset,](https://substack.com/redirect/bdd8e157-8910-4faa-9962-52149d9ff108?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** prompting the board to **[open an independent investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/c3680f14-30aa-4126-b281-71062e3ac55f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while keeping him as CEO.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Huang staff admission:** Told employees "I was unfaithful to my wife," remains in place pending the independent directors' review of national-security concerns raised in weekend reports.
* **Board position:** Said it has "no reason to believe" national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised; Huang stays CEO during the inquiry.
* **Alice Huang role:** MegaSpeed executive at the Singapore cloud firm previously probed for helping China obtain Nvidia chips; Beijing rejected the spy claims as unsubstantiated.
* **Market and political reaction:** Stock on track to lose more than $230 billion in market value; Trump called Huang "honorable"; bipartisan lawmakers seeking scrutiny, with a House briefing set for Nov. 18.

# [Futures rise as oil drops on Trump Iran peace signal](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
U.S. stock futures rose Monday as oil prices fell on hopes for Iran talks, with dip buyers **[shrugging off the Nvidia probe](https://substack.com/redirect/5854439a-5f84-4505-bd96-fefa1288dcf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Futures levels:** **[S&P futures up 0.9%](https://substack.com/redirect/1719f082-9285-4945-9847-ad0971992796?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and Dow futures up 1.1%; 10-year yield steady at 4.86%.
* **Oil slide:** WTI down 3.5% to $87.66 and Brent down 3.8% to $94.59 on Iran-talk hopes.
* **Nvidia drag:** Shares down 4-5% premarket on the board probe, yet broader indexes still pointed higher.
* **Broader tape:** Dow later rallied roughly 500 points as oil continued to slide and rotation out of AI into cyclicals continued.

# [Hyperscalers stack $296B debt as $685B comes due by 2027](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman tallies hyperscaler **[lease and purchase commitments at $1.7 trillion](https://substack.com/redirect/66d30ca0-3535-453c-9e3b-7e10db7b6f2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and $1.9 trillion, with $685 billion due by the end of 2027, as year-to-date issuance already exceeds full-year forecasts.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Off-balance sheet:** ZeroHedge's tracker hits $4.1 trillion (up $1 trillion in 90 days) versus $1.0 trillion of on-balance-sheet debt and leases.
* **Issuance pace:** Five deals totaling $67 billion since Oct. 29 pushed Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle year-to-date issuance to $296 billion versus Goldman's $250 billion full-year forecast.
* **Spread risk:** AI-related spread risks tilt toward more widening into early December after the heavy issuance.
* **Capex context:** **[Debt-financed share of hyperscaler capex](https://substack.com/redirect/43d04e15-ff4d-4e00-bec1-d374d9d710ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** expected near 36% in 2026, with issuance peaking around $470 billion in 2028.

# [Hedge funds slash leverage hardest since Covid crash](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
U.S. fundamental long-short funds made their **[largest weekly cut in gross leverage since Covid](https://substack.com/redirect/dc828c19-6cdf-4ae3-8d60-f92f9d0cfc62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and biggest net cut since Liberation Day as AI-linked names were sold, leaving net leverage at five-year lows.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Leverage drop:** Gross leverage fell to 207.5% (26th percentile over the past year); net leverage now at five-year lows.
* **AI selling:** **[AI stocks net sold for a sixth straight session;](https://substack.com/redirect/7c435bce-e4f9-4b6d-b626-b323de99d200?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** trailing 20-day pace of global AI stock selling by hedge funds is the largest in more than five years (−3.0 standard deviations).
* **Tech focus:** Information technology was the most net-sold global sector, with the week's percentage selling on par with the largest net-selling weeks on record since 2016.
* **Positioning note:** Net leverage reduction is still nowhere near levels seen earlier this year during the Iran war; gross rose month-over-month due to mark-to-market effects.

# [Bitcoin slides to $73,500 as Strategy buys more underwater](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bitcoin **[fell to roughly $73,500 over the weekend](https://substack.com/redirect/58a7236e-36fa-49bd-8ff9-cc86a89ea019?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after $1.28 billion in weekly ETF outflows, even as Strategy added another 1,036 coins and took its holding past 850,000.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Strategy purchase:** **[Bought 1,036 bitcoin last week](https://substack.com/redirect/a833ba95-d125-482b-b289-ecffd7b781e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (about $82 million) while spending more than double that amount repurchasing STRC preferred shares.

* **Broader crypto:** Ether and XRP also slid; crypto stocks fell despite the Strategy buy.

# [Goldman panic index reaches 9.57 after midterm relief fade](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman's Vol Panic Index printed 9.57 on Nov. 5,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/aa791f92-0c56-4429-9111-b2e08ea5b515?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[returning to the panic zone with the largest two-day swing in series history](https://substack.com/redirect/aa791f92-0c56-4429-9111-b2e08ea5b515?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after clients unwound protection mid-week and left the market underhedged into Thursday's drop.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49086087-9d72-4308-bbb9-6f835bbe5a68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

* **Underhedged setup:** Clients aggressively cut protection during Wednesday's relief rally, exposing the tape to Thursday's reversal.
* **Mag7 demand:** Mag7 three-month put skew sits in the 89th percentile, showing concentrated downside hedging.
* **Correlation:** Nasdaq top-100 three-month implied correlation is back near Liberation Day peaks at 35.1%.

Goldman's top tech specialist **[said the Nasdaq 100 is re-testing its base trendline](https://substack.com/redirect/aefa47eb-3358-4e69-bdbf-ad00c7b1f88d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/aefa47eb-3358-4e69-bdbf-ad00c7b1f88d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)from the April 2025 and March 2026 lows after a roughly 5% weekly drop, its fourth straight weekly loss.

* **SOX damage:** The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 28% over 22 days.

* **Broader note:** A break would mark a deeper structural shift for the AI-led tape.

name: Rebecca and the Kiros for Congress Team
subject: No Words but Thank You
body:
From the bottom of our hearts
| |
---
| Peter, It’s been over a year since Melat announced her campaign for Congress. In that year, this powerful community came together, made up of thousands of people who care deeply about our city and about our country—a community that believes a better world is possible and is willing to show up, day after day, to make that world a reality. Just about one week ago, we elected Melat Kiros to congress. **236,048 of us showed up to say that we are ready for a new generation of leadership** which will fight to get big money out of politics, pass universal healthcare and childcare, abolish ICE, and end funding for genocidal wars abroad. This is just the beginning for our movement. Building our power will depend on all of us continuing to show up for our community, particularly for those targeted by the harmful conservative ballot measures which threaten the dignity, safety and joy of our trans neighbors and children. The losses only emphasize the urgency of the work ahead here in Colorado, and **to all of the trans kids across this state, we want you to know that you are loved, you belong here, and we will keep fighting for you.** Melat said from the beginning that this campaign was about more than any one person or election, and Tuesday proved that. Here in Denver, we succeeded in passing 7A, 2H, 2I, 2J, 4A, 311 and electing Melissa Mejia to City Council while securing a graduated income tax and additional revenue for our public schools and saying no to police/ICE collaboration at the state wide level. You all helped make these wins possible. **You all dared to believe that we could have stronger, more progressive representation, and then you did something about it.** You knocked 140,000 doors throughout this campaign, 20,000 doors in the last month alone. You made over 500,000 phone calls, canvassed your neighbors, tabled events, and found community members and helped them vote. You built websites, designed stickers, created videos, trained volunteers, checked the inbox, and so so so much more. You all made the impossible possible, and you proved what we have been speaking into existence all along: that organized people beat organized money. To each of the 8,000+ volunteers who knocked doors, made phone calls, tabled events and talked to your friends and family about this movement: The many victories on Tuesday were only possible because of your hard work and dedication. **From the bottom of our hearts, thank you.** We are endlessly grateful and can't wait to keep building with you. Love, Rebecca, Ellis, Casey, Melat and everyone on Team Kiros for Congress

_Top news and headlines from around the state, brought to you by The Robinson Report._
If you missed it Friday, I wrote a long one on what Tuesday did to Maine Republicans. It starts with Thucydides and the Athenians drinking bloody water at the Assinarus River, and it ends with three options for Maine conservatives: whine about it, get better at politics, or move to New Hampshire. In between is the 2022 autopsy nobody read -- that is, nobody working in the profitable parts of Maine's Republican Party. All of it has aged like fine wine, and the prescriptions are now stronger and sharper. **[Read "Blood and Mire in the Kennebec River" here.](https://substack.com/redirect/9dc2f617-439e-4025-8ff8-9aafb534d694?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
#### **[Augusta Starts the CD2 Ranked-Choice Count at 10 a.m.](https://substack.com/redirect/0337790b-13dc-4f7b-9296-c5c746192d71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Secretary of State's office starts the 2nd District tabulation at 10 a.m. today at Department of Public Safety headquarters. It's open to the public and livestreamed on the Secretary of State's YouTube channel. With Paul LePage at 49.9% (170,265 votes) and Matt Dunlap at 48.3% (164,845), the state is required to go through the expensive process of an RCV tabulation; however, Dunlap conceded Thursday. Given that Secretary of State Shenna Bellows is perhaps the least trustworthy public official to ever hold office in Maine, there's some warranted concern that she might magically find a thumb drive with more votes for Dunlap, just like she magically found some more UOCAVA votes that tipped a Kennebec County Commissioner's race, the Oxford County Sheriff's race, and an Oxford County State Senate race.
> **Augusta counts slowly. We don't.[Subscribe free at RobinsonReport.Substack.com](https://substack.com/redirect/8a6d06f2-4b53-49b0-8cfa-16a11cee2f6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..nhtZ3UBJWuAyYo2_cCeUSCIe5Lw7CPBMKRdm_wEgCP0?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=224142452)
#### **[Heating Oil Holds Above $6 a Gallon](https://substack.com/redirect/bd909c2c-ffd9-4425-8221-f8af50538f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
More than 300,000 Maine households rely on heating oil, and the first fill-up of the season is going to hurt. The state Department of Energy Resources' weekly survey has come in above $6 a gallon three weeks running. The newest one, from Nov. 2, puts the statewide average at $6.01, about 79% above last year's $3.35, or roughly $730 more to fill a standard 275-gallon tank. The politicians who've spent 30 years waging war on the fossil fuel industry claim the cause is the war in Iran -- and last week's election results suggest that perhaps voters believe them!
#### **[After Stunning Rout, Maine Republicans Pick Old Leaders to Plot Path Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/a0ebfbd3-9cc2-432e-b6c7-5a8f80cb8b35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Republican lawmakers who survived the blue wave met in Augusta Friday to pick leaders, and they went with experience. The 11-member Senate caucus, down three seats (four, depending on how you account for ex-Republican Rick Bennett), kept Sen. Trey Stewart of Aroostook as leader and tapped Sen. David Haggan of Penobscot as whip. House Republicans, who fall from 73 seats to 61, chose Ken Fredette of Newport as minority leader and Alicia Collins of Sidney as his assistant. Fredette is the pick that matters most. He was a top Republican on Appropriations last session and led the House GOP from the 2012 elections through 2018. He's been working campaigns since Bob Dole's 1988 run. Senate Democrats have 24 seats, enough to pass emergency bills without a single Republican vote. House Democrats, at 90, fall short of two-thirds, so Fredette's 61 can still block emergency measures, bonds and constitutional amendments, but only if they hang together and show up. _(Editor 's note: My story Friday incorrectly labeled Fredette as the GOP lead on Appropriations. A reader helpfully corrects me that the Republican lead was, in fact, Rep. Jack Ducharme of Madison.)_
#### **[Trump Tells 60 Minutes His Deportation Policy "Might Be Too Tough"](https://substack.com/redirect/26617338-af21-47af-964e-ae24c38c1ed5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Despondent conservatives are suffering whiplash. First came Tuesday's election results, then the news that MAGA hero Stephen Miller would become President Donald Trump's new Chief of Staff, then a bizarre 60 Minutes interview with correspondent Ross Douthat in which President Donald Trump appeared to support amnesty for illegal aliens. In an interview CBS aired Sunday, Douthat asked whether the immigration crackdown hurt him in the midterms. "I think it both helped and hurt," Trump said. He gave himself an A+ for closing the border, then added: "But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs." When Douthat asked whether his deportation policy went too far, Trump said, "I think it might be too tough, yeah."
Asked to name one thing he'd like to work on with the new Democratic majority, he'd said, "I'd love to do something on immigration." Asked what a deal would look like, Trump said "the deal would be we would work something out," and called it "something that's actually doable." Then he described "a group of people that I would say on the sort of pretty far right that would like everybody taken out." Douthat asked: "do any of those people work in your administration?" Trump: "Yes." Another camp, Trump said, wants to get the criminals out and let people who've been here "10 and 15 years" work a deal. CBS says the interview was recorded three days after the election. That Friday, Trump named Stephen Miller his chief of staff. The full transcript is at CBS News, and so is [the extended video](https://substack.com/redirect/9c87cf3c-12de-4165-85e8-82492c82e170?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
#### **[These Maine Towns Flipped for Troy Jackson](https://substack.com/redirect/b46d5015-11cf-4866-839d-6974567ea6e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Lewiston, Bangor and Auburn are a big part of why Sen. Susan Collins' historic career has come to an end. A Maine Monitor analysis of election returns counts 45 municipalities that backed Collins in 2020 and Jackson this year. Lewiston went from Collins by 2 to Jackson by 8, and Auburn from Collins by 8 to Jackson by 5. Bangor, where Collins held her election-night party, went from a Collins win of under a point to Jackson by 16. Even where she won, she slipped: little Newburgh went from a 40-point Collins margin to about 33. Matt Junker and Kristian Moravec of The Maine Monitor have [the story](https://substack.com/redirect/b46d5015-11cf-4866-839d-6974567ea6e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
#### **[Lewiston Records 36 Shots-Fired Incidents, 138 Overdoses in First 10 Months of 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/266d958b-ee36-44af-b818-1d4922604f48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Lewiston Police Department's own monthly numbers show gunfire was routine this year and traffic enforcement mostly wasn't. Through October the city logged 36 confirmed shots-fired incidents (nine in April alone) and 138 overdoses (27 in July). Traffic stops fell from 775 in May to 359 in October, and written citations from 190 in April to 37. The reports don't say why enforcement dropped, how many shootings led to arrests, or how many overdoses were fatal. Jon Fetherston has [the story](https://substack.com/redirect/266d958b-ee36-44af-b818-1d4922604f48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
#### **[Showdown: Maine, National Popular Vote Compact and the Compact Clause](https://substack.com/redirect/9899b292-4846-4c58-9e96-1cb36a4e5d92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The compact Maine joined in 2024 would someday hand the state's presidential electoral votes to whoever wins the national tally, 2nd District included. Member states now total 209 electoral votes, 61 short of the 270 that switches it on, and Jonathan Reisman argues the blue wave makes 270 likely before 2028. His case is that the Constitution's Compact Clause means Congress should have to vote on it. He says Collins and LePage both passed when he asked them to push the issue.
#### **[Gorham Voters Approve $6.7 Million Bond for High School Infrastructure Improvements](https://substack.com/redirect/5f8ce89e-a78b-4251-a991-e9e997db894a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Gorham property owners just bought the high school $6.7 million in repairs. Voters approved the bond 5,803 to 3,756, about 60-40. The biggest piece, $4.6 million, replaces six portable classrooms that have been in use for 35 years after being built to last about 15. The district says it was told not to expect state renovation money for 10 to 15 years. Libby Palanza has the story.
#### **[York Woman Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison After Biting Victim Multiple Times During Home Invasion](https://substack.com/redirect/08626f7d-4475-4f57-94e6-b1af89e79e63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Kinley MacDonald, 45, of York, broke into a Parsonsfield home after midnight in August 2022 carrying a revolver, duct tape and a camouflage mask. She bit the homeowner several times and fired a round through a wall. Her DNA on the gun and in the bite marks tied her to it, and investigators say she'd prowled the area for three days and admitted other break-ins in a private Facebook group. She got 28 years with eight suspended, then eight years of probation. Seamus Othot has the story.
#### **[Indian Illegal Sentenced to Nine Years After Scamming Elderly People Across Multiple States](https://substack.com/redirect/51d62249-c02d-4fac-b1cd-86ef8d8c02e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Prakashkumar Prajapati, 47, of India, got nine years in federal court in Portland and must repay $1,897,386. His crew posed as government officials, had elderly victims in five states withdraw cash and buy gold, then sent someone to collect it. The FBI arrested a co-conspirator in the act of picking up a package from a Maine victim. If an elderly parent gets a call from "the government" asking for gold, hang up for them. Seamus Othot has [the story](https://substack.com/redirect/51d62249-c02d-4fac-b1cd-86ef8d8c02e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
#### **[Maine Communities Plan Veterans Day Parades and Ceremonies for Nov. 11](https://substack.com/redirect/08582f8d-b96b-452d-b666-70edd92f0af2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Wednesday is Veterans Day. Saco-Biddeford, Portland and Bangor-Brewer all hold parades. Portland steps off from Longfellow Square at 10:30 a.m. and heads down Congress Street to City Hall, so expect road closures. The Bangor-Brewer parade, run by Bangor High School JROTC, starts at 10:15 a.m. on Vista Way in Brewer and crosses the Joshua Chamberlain Bridge into downtown Bangor, and the Bangor Area Breakfast Rotary's pancake breakfast beforehand at 53 Center St. in Brewer is free for veterans. Jon Fetherston has the full list, Falmouth to Caribou.
### How did we get here
In "Blood and Mire" I put the start of the Republicans' slide in the Covid years, when Gov. Janet Mills used federal money and no-bid contracts to build a political machine that helped re-elect her in 2022. The clearest case is Gateway Community Services -- the Medicaid fraud hydra whose political arm, the Community Organizing Alliance, remains alive and well even as ex-CEO Abdullahi Ali is on the lam in Africa.
Gateway started out billing MaineCare for translation and grew into a Medicaid agency doing about $5 million a year. It was audited three times and found to have overbilled every time. In April, DHHS records obtained through a Freedom of Access Act request showed it had repaid just $118,431.58 of the more than $1.6 million the state says it overbilled. Despite all the improper payments, the Mills Administration shoveled even more cash to the so-called "migrant services" agency. Beginning in 2022, Gateway took no-bid "community health outreach" contracts from the Mills Administration while also running the Community Organizing Alliance, a political group set up to turn out non-English-speaking voters for Maine Democrats in Portland and Lewiston.
Gateway lost its state money, and Ali lost his Falmouth house to the bank. But the Community Organizing Alliance can still be found hustling voters from vans into Lewiston City Hall. In this episode I walk Tom Shattuck through the whole thing: the audits, Ali's presidential campaign (warlord campaign?) in Jubaland, Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland) working at Gateway while she sat in the Legislature, whistleblower Chris Bernardini's timesheet allegations, and the $400,000 in opioid settlement money Attorney General Aaron Frey's office handed the agency. This podcast is the Rosetta Stone to understanding how machine politics works in Maine.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4df97db7-b2de-496c-819d-ab8c811c9a94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Videos from @TheMaineWire on X**
**[Jon checks on a home-care client and gets told he can't come in](https://substack.com/redirect/f8a15e23-d7e8-4bf3-a3c2-4d71e8b6c318?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** : Jon goes back with a cousin to check on a disabled woman living with home-care support, and staff tell him he isn't allowed in her own apartment. Once he's inside, there's no bed, not much furniture and not much food. In the video, Jon says the provider has billed the state more than $78 million since 2019. Maine Republicans pick old hands to lead two shrunken caucuses, LePage's CD2 win moves through useless RCV count, and Trump angers MAGA with amnesty talk Nov 9 | | | | | | | | | | | Top news and headlines from around the state, brought to you by The Robinson Report. If you missed it Friday, I wrote a long one on what Tuesday did to Maine Republicans. It starts with Thucydides and the Athenians drinking bloody water at the Assinarus River, and it ends with three options for Maine conservatives: whine about it, get better at politics, or move to New Hampshire. In between is the 2022 autopsy nobody read -- that is, nobody working in the profitable parts of Maine's Republican Party. All of it has aged like fine wine, and the prescriptions are now stronger and sharper. The Secretary of State's office starts the 2nd District tabulation at 10 a.m. today at Department of Public Safety headquarters. It's open to the public and livestreamed on the Secretary of State's YouTube channel. With Paul LePage at 49.9% (170,265 votes) and Matt Dunlap at 48.3% (164,845), the state is required to go through the expensive process of an RCV tabulation; however, Dunlap conceded Thursday. Given that Secretary of State Shenna Bellows is perhaps the least trustworthy public official to ever hold office in Maine, there's some warranted concern that she might magically find a thumb drive with more votes for Dunlap, just like she magically found some more UOCAVA votes that tipped a Kennebec County Commissioner's race, the Oxford County Sheriff's race, and an Oxford County State Senate race. Augusta counts slowly. We don't. More than 300,000 Maine households rely on heating oil, and the first fill-up of the season is going to hurt. The state Department of Energy Resources' weekly survey has come in above $6 a gallon three weeks running. The newest one, from Nov. 2, puts the statewide average at $6.01, about 79% above last year's $3.35, or roughly $730 more to fill a standard 275-gallon tank. The politicians who've spent 30 years waging war on the fossil fuel industry claim the cause is the war in Iran -- and last week's election results suggest that perhaps voters believe them! The Republican lawmakers who survived the blue wave met in Augusta Friday to pick leaders, and they went with experience. The 11-member Senate caucus, down three seats (four, depending on how you account for ex-Republican Rick Bennett), kept Sen. Trey Stewart of Aroostook as leader and tapped Sen. David Haggan of Penobscot as whip. House Republicans, who fall from 73 seats to 61, chose Ken Fredette of Newport as minority leader and Alicia Collins of Sidney as his assistant. Fredette is the pick that matters most. He was a top Republican on Appropriations last session and led the House GOP from the 2012 elections through 2018. He's been working campaigns since Bob Dole's 1988 run. Senate Democrats have 24 seats, enough to pass emergency bills without a single Republican vote. House Democrats, at 90, fall short of two-thirds, so Fredette's 61 can still block emergency measures, bonds and constitutional amendments, but only if they hang together and show up. (Editor 's note: My story Friday incorrectly labeled Fredette as the GOP lead on Appropriations. A reader helpfully corrects me that the Republican lead was, in fact, Rep. Jack Ducharme of Madison.) Despondent conservatives are suffering whiplash. First came Tuesday's election results, then the news that MAGA hero Stephen Miller would become President Donald Trump's new Chief of Staff, then a bizarre 60 Minutes interview with correspondent Ross Douthat in which President Donald Trump appeared to support amnesty for illegal aliens. In an interview CBS aired Sunday, Douthat asked whether the immigration crackdown hurt him in the midterms. "I think it both helped and hurt," Trump said. He gave himself an A+ for closing the border, then added: "But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs." When Douthat asked whether his deportation policy went too far, Trump said, "I think it might be too tough, yeah." Asked to name one thing he'd like to work on with the new Democratic majority, he'd said, "I'd love to do something on immigration." Asked what a deal would look like, Trump said "the deal would be we would work something out," and called it "something that's actually doable." Then he described "a group of people that I would say on the sort of pretty far right that would like everybody taken out." Douthat asked: "do any of those people work in your administration?" Trump: "Yes." Another camp, Trump said, wants to get the criminals out and let people who've been here "10 and 15 years" work a deal. CBS says the interview was recorded three days after the election. That Friday, Trump named Stephen Miller his chief of staff. The full transcript is at CBS News, and so is . Lewiston, Bangor and Auburn are a big part of why Sen. Susan Collins' historic career has come to an end. A Maine Monitor analysis of election returns counts 45 municipalities that backed Collins in 2020 and Jackson this year. Lewiston went from Collins by 2 to Jackson by 8, and Auburn from Collins by 8 to Jackson by 5. Bangor, where Collins held her election-night party, went from a Collins win of under a point to Jackson by 16. Even where she won, she slipped: little Newburgh went from a 40-point Collins margin to about 33. Matt Junker and Kristian Moravec of The Maine Monitor have . The Lewiston Police Department's own monthly numbers show gunfire was routine this year and traffic enforcement mostly wasn't. Through October the city logged 36 confirmed shots-fired incidents (nine in April alone) and 138 overdoses (27 in July). Traffic stops fell from 775 in May to 359 in October, and written citations from 190 in April to 37. The reports don't say why enforcement dropped, how many shootings led to arrests, or how many overdoses were fatal. Jon Fetherston has . The compact Maine joined in 2024 would someday hand the state's presidential electoral votes to whoever wins the national tally, 2nd District included. Member states now total 209 electoral votes, 61 short of the 270 that switches it on, and Jonathan Reisman argues the blue wave makes 270 likely before 2028. His case is that the Constitution's Compact Clause means Congress should have to vote on it. He says Collins and LePage both passed when he asked them to push the issue. Gorham property owners just bought the high school $6.7 million in repairs. Voters approved the bond 5,803 to 3,756, about 60-40. The biggest piece, $4.6 million, replaces six portable classrooms that have been in use for 35 years after being built to last about 15. The district says it was told not to expect state renovation money for 10 to 15 years. Libby Palanza has the story. Kinley MacDonald, 45, of York, broke into a Parsonsfield home after midnight in August 2022 carrying a revolver, duct tape and a camouflage mask. She bit the homeowner several times and fired a round through a wall. Her DNA on the gun and in the bite marks tied her to it, and investigators say she'd prowled the area for three days and admitted other break-ins in a private Facebook group. She got 28 years with eight suspended, then eight years of probation. Seamus Othot has the story. Prakashkumar Prajapati, 47, of India, got nine years in federal court in Portland and must repay $1,897,386. His crew posed as government officials, had elderly victims in five states withdraw cash and buy gold, then sent someone to collect it. The FBI arrested a co-conspirator in the act of picking up a package from a Maine victim. If an elderly parent gets a call from "the government" asking for gold, hang up for them. Seamus Othot has . Wednesday is Veterans Day. Saco-Biddeford, Portland and Bangor-Brewer all hold parades. Portland steps off from Longfellow Square at 10:30 a.m. and heads down Congress Street to City Hall, so expect road closures. The Bangor-Brewer parade, run by Bangor High School JROTC, starts at 10:15 a.m. on Vista Way in Brewer and crosses the Joshua Chamberlain Bridge into downtown Bangor, and the Bangor Area Breakfast Rotary's pancake breakfast beforehand at 53 Center St. in Brewer is free for veterans. The clearest case is Gateway Community Services -- the Medicaid fraud hydra whose political arm, the Community Organizing Alliance, remains alive and well even as ex-CEO Abdullahi Ali is on the lam in Africa. Gateway lost its state money, and Ali lost his Falmouth house to the bank. But the Community Organizing Alliance can still be found hustling voters from vans into Lewiston City Hall. # Monday, November 9, 2026
---
**Dear Reader,** Today we're releasing our first book: [_The Flyover Book of Trivia 2027_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJys0LFO8zAUBeCnsbdG9167cT14-H-hqANFbEgskV3ftAYnrhIrETw9Kgs8APPR-XR0Xk79yaecpsuTH9nVofSRYzr7yrGfeFsy18pzX6885I-y8hxKeS9DndOafE9A7Q5xB_ZXDWV0AzOxkuzQWE17OBgjr44M7wOBVWjQIFuz18ZaABVVG4ImmdxdRASLFhBNEw8GhsigQxsCKBYaOKZa5uatpOlnVXMuo8zuWuttEeqfoE5Qt21b40f_WaZ7LKiLN0Hdfzg-vx4ej-2DnF28bSnntLRGaLiMPuVvqf7VE6ujrwAAAP__Bb91Ng).

Every edition of _The Flyover_ ends with a trivia question. Over the past three years, we've written hundreds of them, so our editors went back through the archive and picked the 100 we liked best. Not the ones you've heard a hundred times. The ones that made us stop and say, wait, really?
[](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJys0LFO8zAUBeCnsbdG9167cT14-H-hqANFbEgskV3ftAYnrhIrETw9Kgs8APPR-XR0Xk79yaecpsuTH9nVofSRYzr7yrGfeFsy18pzX6885I-y8hxKeS9DndOafE9A7Q5xB_ZXDWV0AzOxkuzQWE17OBgjr44M7wOBVWjQIFuz18ZaABVVG4ImmdxdRASLFhBNEw8GhsigQxsCKBYaOKZa5uatpOlnVXMuo8zuWuttEeqfoE5Qt21b40f_WaZ7LKiLN0Hdfzg-vx4ej-2DnF28bSnntLRGaLiMPuVvqf7VE6ujrwAAAP__Bb91Ng) A few to get you going:

* Which president made the White House staff hide from him?
* A Post Office loophole once let Americans mail what?
* Neil Armstrong left part of his spacesuit on the moon. What was it?
* Which household fixture holds a Guinness speed record of 116 mph?

Every answer comes with a full-color illustration and the story behind the fact. A few also come with a QR code for the things we couldn't fit on paper, like the color of a Martian sunset or a recording of the early Rolling Stones singing a Rice Krispies jingle. An index at the back lets you round up every question on presidents, food, inventions, the sky, and more.

We had a lot of fun putting this together, and we hope you enjoy thumbing through it. It's a book for the guest room, the coffee table, or a long drive--and it's full of fun surprises. If you have a _Flyover_ reader in your life, it would make a great Christmas gift. | | Peter, This morning, Donald Trump posted this about last week's elections — the ones where four of our five Indigenous women made history: [](https://go.indigenouswomenleadpac.com/f/a/P0YaRNTyTMt8AEkXIcjFaw~~/AAUS1hA~/vON5tkd2GdlquasRf3TsDSfIQLcSMeYgi1iwqMPwyfqViQlAjiyQa_Jl9yzKI11wYlY6ryEhghifbtN5E2JwRgkLA_fsLoI2BupdYFDwc_2yW7Wrt3LqOo8MB5wmiFnizORNbulLVprPhrISjC4DDd1Rvo4f4VSrETgfRtvEmgbb8G0wYGXCqUzwd3tZCw5j3jGq_mZUTDAmZXrepCjJfOO1gmvQ87UTTAByWAtyLd4d-ihP0q4DwB058w2aPwcbM1pwgSwvK2IqzI1pLXd7gXe4QlOnLO6EJSWUSO19asJ-JdPUzAMWkiai2yzcK0In9dG9M7rOsA1fF0teHSxRbg~~) This is unsurprising. We’ve seen it before from him. But there are exactly **two** uncalled Senate races left in America. One of them is Alaska — where **Mary Peltola leads by roughly 600 votes** , where Trump's own Justice Department already sued to block certification if she wins, where that suit's appeal is still alive, and where the other side built a recount fund on Election Day itself. Five days ago, Trump said he wouldn't challenge the results. This morning, he's questioning the entire election. We're not going to pretend to know his next move. We don't have to. The job is the same whatever comes: **count every ballot, answer every filing, and build a margin that ends the argument.** Four Indigenous women have already won their races. Hi, it's Troy Jackson. I'm sharing a note from my friend, Scott Colom, because the stakes couldn't be higher now that we have the chance to strengthen our Senate majority and meaningfully check Trump and his MAGA agenda. Will you read it, then **[split $15 between us?](https://substack.com/redirect/d3071cee-c827-4cb3-99c4-30921095cfab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bcf2e41f-2950-44ea-a33b-bfa663aa3f78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Hey,

Something I've been really proud of over the last week has been the rest of the country learning a thing or two about Mississippi and who we are. We are a beautiful state with wonderful people.

**Mississippi matters. Everybody better get used to hearing that.**

Last week, hundreds of thousands of voters in all 82 counties came together to say they wanted to pick a senator who represented _THEM_ , not the billionaires.

We owe it to them to make sure that the rest of this process plays out smoothly.

We need to count every lawful vote, and protect the will of the people. I'm so proud of all our team has done so far to make that happen, but there's still a lot of work in front of us -- and we have serious budget needs we have to meet.

I will always stand up and fight for Mississippi. Now, for just a little bit longer, I'm asking you to stand with me.

**[Can you please make a donation of $5 or even $25 to help us win the Mississippi Senate race? This could be the most closely divided race in modern history, so anything you can give makes a major difference.](https://substack.com/redirect/b433aa53-0e30-4af5-977f-562f7d45d577?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ CONTRIBUTE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/b433aa53-0e30-4af5-977f-562f7d45d577?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for everything you're doing,
Scott Colom

body:
We can still win here in NC-03

Peter, Almost one week later, I am still buzzing from election day and election night. We have all put in a LOT of hard work over the course of this campaign. But hard work is good work – and the work isn’t quite done. **At this point, we are still down 233 votes, but that number will change very soon.** The State Board of Elections is reporting that thousands of ballots across our district are still being tallied. # **Join Our Autism Support Group Tomorrow**
---
|
---
| You are invited to join us for our next **Autism Support Group Tomorrow, November 10th at 4:30 PM PST / 7:30 PM EST via Zoom**. Our monthly support group is a welcoming space for parents, caregivers, and families impacted by autism to come together, connect, and learn from one another. This is an opportunity to **ask questions, share experiences, hear parent testimonials, exchange resources, and receive encouragement** from a community that understands the challenges and victories that can come with the autism journey. At Autism Health, we believe families need more than information. They need **connection, support, and a community where they feel heard**. Whether your family is navigating a new diagnosis or you have been on this journey for many years, you are welcome to join us. **Advance registration is required to attend.** Once registered, you will receive the Zoom information for the meeting. We look forward to seeing you and continuing to build a strong and supportive Autism Health community!
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/icKlyAqftkh?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")
---
|
---
|
# **Join Us for Our Annual Gala in California!**
---
|
---
| Join us for an unforgettable evening of elegance, inspiration, and purpose at the **Transforming Lives Annual Gala: Lighting the Path to Solutions!** Hosted by Autism Health. This special event will bring together philanthropists, community leaders, healthcare professionals, and advocates who share a commitment to advancing research, education, and innovative solutions for individuals with autism and their families. We invite you to be part of this extraordinary evening at the beautiful **Sherwood Country Club in Thousand Oaks, California** , while taking advantage of our exclusive **Early Bird ticket and table pricing, available through November 30, 2026!** **Date:** Saturday, January 30, 2027 **Location: Sherwood Country Club**
[320 W Stafford Road](https://us.list-manage.com/8kklsV750ly?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332)
[Thousand Oaks, CA 91361](https://us.list-manage.com/5psy3M39kwx?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332) **VIP Reception:** 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM
**General Admission:** 6:00 PM – 10:30 PM **Dress Code:** Formal Attire/Black-Tie For a limited time, we're offering **exclusive Early Bird discounts on all tickets and tables!** Take advantage of these special savings now through November 30, 2026. **Prices increase December 1st!** **General Admission:** ~~$650~~ , **now $550**
_Save $100!_
**VIP Admission:** ~~$1,050~~ , **now $950**
_Save $100!_
**General Admission Table of 10:** ~~$6,000~~ , **now**** $5,000**
_Save $1,000!_
**VIP Table of 10:** ~~$10,000~~ , **now****$9,000**
_Save $1,000!_ **Don't wait! Secure your tickets or reserve your table today before Early Bird pricing ends November 30th!** We are honored to feature **General Michael Flynn, Del Bigtree, Nick Vujicic, Dr. Sabine Hazan, and Dr. Brian Hooker** , with additional special guests and speakers to be announced. Guests will enjoy an elegant evening featuring exceptional dining, drinks, live entertainment, inspiring presentations, and exciting **live and silent auctions** , all while supporting a cause that is close to our hearts. **Sponsorship opportunities are also available for businesses and individuals who want to make an even greater impact.** Please contact Tracy for more information at [**tracy@autismhealth.com**](mailto:tracy@autismhealth.com). Thank you for your continued support, generosity, and belief in our mission. We look forward to celebrating with you in Thousand Oaks as we light the path to solutions and work together to transform lives!
