DHS Sec Mullin reportedly tells Politico he is open to a bipartisan immigration deal that could include permanent legal status for DACA recipients: "Amnesty is never going to be a solution. We're never going to allow amnesty to happen. So that's a full stop."
| 7:32 PM * Nov 9, 2026 * 5.47K Views20 Replies * 15 Reposts * 25 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/3aca69e4-eda7-4d0a-9df3-9d2f7c65bf61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Mullin said he 's open to legislative action giving DACA recipients permanent legal status** but insisted current enforcement policy won't change, adding that Trump has encouraged him to engage with Democrats who've reached out about potential cooperation.
* **The remarks drew sharp criticism from immigration hawks,** with commentators warning a scaled-back deportation approach could hurt the party, while the White House pushed back on characterizations of Trump's comments as advocating "amnesty," noting the word was never used.

* * *
# **Secret Service subdues combative driver after crash near White House**
Video showed Secret Service agents and National Guard members struggling to detain a driver **[who crashed his car](https://substack.com/redirect/5a0b3fd1-d78b-4057-a381-605ee1a74ba5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** into a sidewalk sign near Lafayette Park Monday morning, with smoke pouring from the vehicle before officers forced him to the ground and arrested him.

Unclear what happened but someone just drove into a sign on the north end of Lafayette Square Park and then fought with Secret Service and National Guard when they got out of their car.

* **A separate individual jumped a barricade near the park 's northwest corner around the same time** and was also arrested, though officials haven't confirmed whether the two incidents were connected.
* **The White House, where President Trump was present, was briefly locked down** and surrounding roads closed following the incidents around 10 a.m. There were reportedly no injuries.

* * *
# **Judge sets 2028 trial date for accused Charlie Kirk killer Tyler Robinson**
A Utah judge rejected Tyler Robinson's request to delay his capital murder trial until 2029, instead setting jury selection **[to begin June 21, 2028,](https://substack.com/redirect/4b93fc41-56d8-4c82-bf58-266ff654b3c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the case over Charlie Kirk's September 2025 assassination.
* **Prosecutors had sought an earlier trial,** with Kirk's widow Erika pushing for an October 2027 start, arguing further delays would prolong her family's distress and allow Robinson's death-penalty defense team -- already billed $1.6 million -- to continue accumulating taxpayer-funded fees.
* **Robinson, 23, faces first-degree murder charges for allegedly shooting Kirk** from a rooftop during a campus speech, reportedly motivated by opposition to Kirk's views on traditional relationships; he's pleaded not guilty and could face execution by firing squad if convicted.

Rep. Thomas Massie triggered **[a forced vote on impeaching Secretary of War Pete Hegseth](https://substack.com/redirect/86c006e3-279f-4a03-84cb-fcdee583df41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by introducing a privileged resolution Monday, requiring House action within two legislative days, with Massie having warned he'd move forward unless Hegseth resigned.

The Election Is Over. Now Comes the Hard Part.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

NOVEMBER 9, 2026

RMV ELECTION REPORT

ONE WEEK AGO, COLORADO VOTERS DELIVERED A MESSAGE. NOW COMES THE
HARDER QUESTION: WHAT ARE WE GOING TO DO WITH IT?

We've spent the last week reporting on historic election results,
congressional losses, and ballot measures that will shape our state's
future.

But today, we want to look forward.

Because while Colorado's political landscape has changed dramatically,
there are lessons to be learned, victories worth celebrating, and
plenty of reasons not to give up on our beautiful state.

🇺🇸 WHAT IDAHO CAN TEACH COLORADO

Last Tuesday's Democratic wave swept across the country, flipping
seats in places Republicans once considered safe. But not
everywhere...

_IDAHO HELD ITS GROUND._

Republicans swept all seven statewide offices, retained their
congressional seats, and maintained veto-proof legislative
supermajorities. Governor Brad Little won reelection by approximately
25 points. Democrats flipped six legislative seats, but Republicans
still retained roughly 84 of the state's 105 seats.

So what made the difference?

Idaho has an _ENORMOUS REPUBLICAN REGISTRATION ADVANTAGE_, but its
results also illustrate the importance of grassroots organization,
strong local party infrastructure, and engaging voters around issues
they care about.

Florida offers another state worth studying as Republicans examine
which political organizations proved most resilient. The credit being
given in Florida is Governor DeSantis' _CRACKDOWN ON VOTER ROLL
CLEANUP_, and a _PROPERTY TAX MEASURE_ that got people to show up to
the ballot box.

The lesson? Political success requires more than showing up every two
years. It takes organization, strong candidates, community engagement,
and the willingness to do the unglamorous work between elections.
That's a conversation Colorado needs to have.

🏛️ THE REAL WORK BEGINS IN JANUARY

Here's one reason that work matters.

Protect Kids Colorado, the grassroots organization led by Erin Lee,
achieved something remarkable last week: Voters approved all three of
its ballot measures.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_PROPOSITION 133
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
strengthened penalties for child sex trafficking. _PROPOSITION 134
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
established sex-based eligibility requirements for girls' and women's
sports. _PROPOSITION 135
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
prohibited certain surgeries on minors intended to alter biological
sex characteristics.

BUT HERE'S THE CATCH: The legislature can amend these voter-approved
laws with a simple majority. Our reporting found that lawmakers had
already killed a narrower version of Proposition 133
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
earlier this year. And Gov.-elect Phil Weiser has raised concerns
about Proposition 134
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
including the possibility of invasive examinations that the measure
itself does not require. Proposition 135 takes effect January 1
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Lawmakers return January 11.

The ballot box was one chapter. What happens at the Capitol will be
the next.

Another important part of our work begins after a ballot measure
passes: following the money.

TAKE PROPOSITION NN.

Voters approved changes to Colorado's TABOR revenue limit that
eliminate expected refunds for at least the next two years. But our
reporting found that the campaign's education funding promises don't
necessarily translate into guaranteed teacher raises.

OR PROPOSITION 137
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
which directs approximately $175 million annually toward conservation
and wildfire-related programs, while leaving lawmakers discretion over
appropriations.

A ballot measure's promises and its legal requirements aren't always
the same thing. And understanding that difference is exactly why
independent reporting matters.

There's no sugarcoating Colorado's congressional results.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Colorado's 5th Congressional District
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
defeating Jeff Crank. And with CD4 still too close to call,
Republicans face the _POSSIBILITY OF EMERGING WITH JUST ONE OF THOSE
FOUR SEATS_.

political organizations, candidates, and voters can learn from those
losses.

the character, knowledge, and civic responsibility of its citizens.

INTO STRENGTHENING OUR COMMUNITIES AS WE ARE INTO WINNING ELECTIONS?_

officials accountable for their promises.

| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---

| | | Peter,
---
_Nadia was only 15 years old when they went looking for her. _ A pastor had called House Parent Project, a children's home in Mexico. He knew Nadia was in danger. He even knew the Metro station in Mexico City where she could often be found.So the house parents went and they found her. But to understand what happened next, you need to know where Nadia came from. She never knew her father. Her mother lived an unstable and dangerous life, moving from one man to another. Nadia was the oldest of three little girls. Her youngest sister was given up for adoption. But Nadia grew up with almost nothing and no one. She survived on the streets of Mexico City, surrounded by drugs, prostitution, abandonment, and exploitation. Imagine being 15 years old and wondering if there is a single adult in this world you can trust. That was the girl they found near that Metro station. There was doubt in Nadia's eyes. But they asked her to give them a chance.

clean_body: A frightened 15-year-old was given a chance. See where she is today. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Peter, Nadia was only 15 years old when they went looking for her. A pastor had called House Parent Project, a children's home in Mexico. He knew Nadia was in danger. He even knew the Metro station in Mexico City where she could often be found.So the house parents went and they found her. But to understand what happened next, you need to know where Nadia came from. She never knew her father. Her mother lived an unstable and dangerous life, moving from one man to another. Nadia was the oldest of three little girls. Her youngest sister was given up for adoption. But Nadia grew up with almost nothing and no one. She survived on the streets of Mexico City, surrounded by drugs, prostitution, abandonment, and exploitation. Imagine being 15 years old and wondering if there is a single adult in this world you can trust. That was the girl they found near that Metro station. There was doubt in Nadia's eyes. But they asked her to give them a chance. They told her something every child deserves to hear: You are loved. They promised to protect her and help her get an education. And Nadia willingly went with them. She left behind a horrible life and came home to parents who would raise her as their own. Peter, Nadia's story is one reason Sound of Freedom Foundation works with groups like House Parent Project.My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the movie Sound of Freedom because after learning what traffickers do to innocent children, I could not simply look away.For me, it stopped being a movie. It became a calling. Today, the Sound of Freedom Foundation carries that mission forward. Our mission is simple: Stop the sale of God 's children. House Parent Project shares that commitment. Their house parents give these children the love and care they've never known. And Nadia shows what can happen when a child is not abandoned. A couple of years after her rescue, the team found Nadia's sister, Sofia. She was suffering through many of the same horrors. They rescued her too. Today, Sofia works full time caring for other children who have experienced the same kinds of brokenness. Then something beautiful happened in Nadia's life. She met Joseph, who had also grown up in the same Village - the House Parent Project community. They fell in love. They married, Joseph became a foreman, and the couple moved away for several years. They welcomed a son and daughter of their own. Yet they kept coming back for Christmas, Mother's Day, and birthdays. Their hearts were still with the children. Finally, in 2019, Nadia and Joseph came home permanently. Today, they are second in command at one of the large children 's homes. The child who once needed someone to find hergrew up to help care for children who need to be found. That isrestoration. That is hope. And that is why I am writing to you. Today, House Parent Project cares for, educates and protects between 130 and 150 children in two homes, every single day. When it is safe, they work to restore children to healthy homes with family members. When that cannot happen, the homes may raise these children as their own until they grow up, get jobs, and go to college. More than 40 children that were residents stayed to become staff after they grew up. Others have grown up and married national pastors and missionaries. But there's a problem. The phone never stops ringing. There is always another child. Another crisis and another need. And the resources are slim. Providing three meals for one child costs about $4 a day. And that doesn't include clothes, shoes, diapers, or all the other things children need. Jesus said: " Let the little children come to me." (Matthew 19:14) I believe we have a duty to hear the cries of children who cannot protect themselves. Because when good people stay quiet, evil has room to grow. But when good people stand together,lives can change. Nadia is living proof. Peter, will you help us stand with House Parent Project and the house parents caring for children like Nadia today? "=" $25 can help feed a child fornearly a week $50 can help feed a child fornearly two weeks $100 can help feed a childfor25 days $200 can help**feedtwo children for 25 days That 's three meals every day. Maybe we cannot answer every call today. But together, we can help answer the next one. Please give now. And please pray for the children and for those caring for them. Share this mission with someone you love. Because this truth must be heard around the world: God 's children are not for sale. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. It costs about $4 to provide one child with three meals for one day. The phone is still ringing, and more children need help. Please stand with us today. | ** Sound of Freedom Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.
